name: Supported Squat
summary: Learn the squat with light hand support for balance and depth.
equipment: counter, doorframe or sturdy chair to hold
startingPosition: Face a counter, a doorframe or the back of a sturdy chair, close enough to hold it with elbows slightly bent. Feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly, eyes forward.
steps: Hold the support lightly with both hands, elbows slightly bent, weight in your feet.
Brace your trunk, then sit your hips back and down as your knees bend and your arms straighten.
Let the support counterbalance you so you can sit back without tipping, not hold you up.
Lower only as far as your heels stay flat and your lower back keeps its natural curve.
Stand up by pushing through your whole foot, with your hands only steadying you.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Sit your hips back and down over two to three seconds, letting your arms straighten as you go.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Push the floor away and stand tall in about one to two seconds, hands still light on the support.

breathing: Breathe in and brace before you lower. Breathe out as you push through the hardest part of standing up.
cues: Push the floor away, don't pull with your arms.
Only as deep as your heels stay down.

formChecks.check: As you stand, your elbows stay almost straight. Elbows bending on the way up means your arms are pulling you up.
Your knees stay over your feet, roughly in line with your second toe, on the way down and on the way up.
At your lowest point, your heels are still flat and your lower back keeps its natural curve.

mistakes.title: Pulling up with the arms
mistakes.looksLike: As you stand, your elbows bend, your shoulders hunch toward the support and your knuckles grip hard.
mistakes.why: Your arms take over the hardest part of the rep, so your legs don't practice standing up on their own.
mistakes.fix: Rest open hands or fingertips on the support and push the floor away with your feet. If you still need to pull, stop a little higher.
mistakes.cue: Hands open, feet push the floor away.

mistakes.title: Heels lifting
mistakes.looksLike: Near the bottom your heels peel off the floor and your weight rolls toward your toes, often while you lean into the support.
mistakes.why: Your balance moves to the front of your feet, and your knees take more of the load than your hips.
mistakes.fix: Keep big toe, little toe and heel down. Let your arms straighten so your hips can sit back, and stop where your heels still stay flat.
mistakes.cue: Arms long, hips back, heels flat.

mistakes.title: Knees collapsing inward
mistakes.looksLike: Seen from the front, your knees drift inside the line of your feet as you lower or as you stand up.
mistakes.why: Your knees end up out of line with your hips and feet, and your glutes do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Keep each knee pointing over your second toe the whole time. Think "spread the floor" with your feet and rise more slowly.
mistakes.cue: Spread the floor, knees over toes.

safety: Check that the support can't slide or tip before you start. A fixed counter or doorframe is steadier than a light chair.
Squat to a depth you can control without pain. If your knees hurt, stay higher and add depth gradually.
Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Hold with both hands and squat only partway
harder: Box Squat

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Standing tall facing a kitchen counter, hands resting lightly on its edge, elbows slightly bent, feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out, eyes forward.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Hips back and down to about knee height, heels flat, knees over the toes, arms nearly straight with hands still resting on the counter edge, chest up, back in its natural curve.

name: Box Squat
summary: A squat to a seat behind you that guides your depth and teaches control.
startingPosition: Stand with your back to a sturdy chair or box, calves about a hand's width from its edge. Feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly, arms reaching forward, eyes forward.
steps: Stand with your back to a sturdy chair or box, calves about a hand's width from its edge.
Brace your trunk and reach your arms forward for balance.
Sit your hips back and down slowly until you lightly touch the seat.
Keep your weight in your feet during the touch, without relaxing onto the seat.
Stand straight back up by pushing through your whole foot, without rocking.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Reach your hips back toward the seat and lower over two to three seconds until you just touch it.

phases.label: Touch
phases.text: Brush the seat for about one second, feet flat and trunk braced, without letting your weight settle.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Push through your whole foot and stand tall in about one to two seconds, on the same path you came down.

breathing: Breathe in and brace before you lower. Keep the brace through the touch, then breathe out as you stand.
cues: Touch the seat, don't land on it.

formChecks.check: At the touch, your torso keeps the same forward lean it had on the way down. No lean back and no thump.
Leaving the seat, your hips and shoulders rise together, with no forward swing of the chest, and your heels stay flat.
Your knees stay in line with your second toe, especially in the first few inches off the seat.

mistakes.title: Dropping onto the seat
mistakes.looksLike: You sit all the way down with a thump: your torso tips back, your weight settles onto the seat and your feet go light on the floor.
mistakes.why: Your legs stop working at the hardest point, and the rep loses the control it is meant to teach.
mistakes.fix: Lower over two to three seconds and just brush the seat. If you can't slow the last few inches, use a higher seat.
mistakes.cue: Lower slowly, just brush the seat.

mistakes.title: Rocking to stand up
mistakes.looksLike: At the bottom you lean back onto the seat, then swing your chest forward to throw your hips off it.
mistakes.why: Momentum does the work your legs should be doing, and you lose the position you built on the way down.
mistakes.fix: Keep your torso angle still at the touch, with your weight in your feet. Push straight up through your whole foot. If you still rock, raise the seat.
mistakes.cue: Torso still, drive straight up.

mistakes.title: Knees collapsing inward
mistakes.looksLike: Seen from the front, your knees drift inside the line of your feet, most often as you leave the seat.
mistakes.why: Your knees move out of line with your hips and feet, and your glutes do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Point each knee over your second toe and think "spread the floor" as you stand. Slow down the first few inches off the seat.
mistakes.cue: Knees over second toes as you stand.

safety: Use a chair or box that can't slide or tip. Set a chair against a wall if it moves.
Pick a seat height you can stand up from without rocking. A higher seat is a fine place to start.
If your knees hurt, raise the seat to shorten the range. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Supported Squat
harder: Bodyweight Squat

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Standing tall with back to a sturdy chair, calves a hand's width from its edge, feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out, arms reaching forward at shoulder height, eyes forward.

frames.label: Touch
frames.pose: Hips back and down, just touching the front edge of the chair seat, thighs about parallel to the floor, heels flat, knees over the toes, chest up with a slight forward lean, arms reaching forward.

name: Bodyweight Squat
summary: Practice sitting down and standing up with control.
startingPosition: Stand tall with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly, arms relaxed or reaching forward for balance.
steps: Stand with feet approximately shoulder-width apart and brace your trunk.
Bend at hips and knees to descend within a comfortable pain-free range.
Keep your whole foot in contact with the floor and knees moving in line with toes.
Stand tall by pushing through your feet.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Sit your hips back and down as your knees bend, taking two to three seconds.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Push through your whole foot to stand back up in about two seconds, breathing out as you rise.

breathing: Breathe in and brace your stomach before you lower. Breathe out as you push through the hardest part of standing up.
cues: Tripod foot: big toe, little toe, heel.
Sit between your heels, not onto your toes.
Only as deep as you can control.

formChecks.check: At the bottom, your shins and your back lean forward by roughly the same angle, and your heels stay flat.
Your knees stay over your feet, roughly in line with your second toe, on the way down and on the way up.
Your lower back keeps its natural curve. Your best depth is just above the point where it starts to round.

mistakes.title: Heels lifting
mistakes.looksLike: Near the bottom your heels peel off the floor and your weight rolls onto the balls of your feet.
mistakes.why: Balance gets shaky and the front of the knees takes more of the load.
mistakes.fix: Keep big toe, little toe and heel on the floor. Squat only as deep as you can with heels down, or use the box squat.
mistakes.cue: Heels down; stop before they lift.

mistakes.title: Knees collapsing inward
mistakes.looksLike: Seen from the front, your knees drift inside the line of your feet as you lower or as you stand up.
mistakes.why: Your knees end up out of line with your hips and feet, and your glutes do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Keep each knee pointing over your second toe the whole time. Think "spread the floor" with your feet and rise more slowly.
mistakes.cue: Knees over second toes, rise slowly.

mistakes.title: Loss of trunk control
mistakes.looksLike: Your chest drops toward your thighs, or your lower back rounds and tucks under at the bottom.
mistakes.why: The work shifts from your legs to your lower back, and the rep gets harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Brace before every rep, keep your chest facing forward, and stop just above the depth where your back starts to round.
mistakes.cue: Brace; stop before your back rounds.

safety: Squat to a depth you can control without pain. Holding a counter for balance is fine while you learn.
If your knees hurt, use a box or chair to limit the depth and swap to the box squat.
easier: Box Squat
harder: Goblet Squat

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Standing tall, feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out, arms relaxed at the sides, eyes forward.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Hips back and down to about knee height, heels flat, knees over the toes, arms reaching forward for balance, chest up.

name: Goblet Squat
summary: A squat with a dumbbell at your chest that adds load and helps you sit upright.
startingPosition: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest, both palms cupping its top end, elbows pointing down. Feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly, eyes forward.
steps: Cup the top end of one dumbbell in both hands and hold it vertically against your chest.
Set your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly, and brace your trunk.
Sit down between your heels, keeping the dumbbell against your chest and your elbows pointing down.
Lower until your elbows are just inside your knees, or as deep as you can control with heels flat.
Stand up by pushing through your whole foot, keeping the dumbbell on your chest.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Sit down between your heels over two to three seconds, dumbbell pinned to your chest.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Push through your whole foot and stand tall in about one to two seconds, dumbbell still on your chest.

breathing: Breathe in and brace before you lower, holding the dumbbell tight. Breathe out as you pass the hardest part of standing up.
cues: Elbows inside your knees at the bottom.
Tripod foot: big toe, little toe, heel.
Choose a weight you can control every rep.

formChecks.check: The dumbbell stays vertical and in contact with your chest from the top of the rep to the bottom.
At the bottom, your elbows sit just inside your knees and your knees stay over your second toes.
At the bottom, your heels are flat and your lower back keeps its natural curve.

mistakes.title: Dumbbell drifting away from chest
mistakes.looksLike: The dumbbell moves forward off your chest and tips, so your arms end up holding it out in front of you.
mistakes.why: Weight further in front pulls your chest down, so your arms and upper back work to hold it and the squat is harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Pin the dumbbell to your chest with your elbows pointing down. If you can't keep it there, use a lighter one.
mistakes.cue: Elbows down, dumbbell pinned to chest.

mistakes.title: Heels lifting
mistakes.looksLike: Near the bottom your heels peel up and your weight rolls toward your toes, often as the dumbbell pulls you forward.
mistakes.why: Your balance shifts forward, and the front of your knees takes more of the load than your hips.
mistakes.fix: Keep big toe, little toe and heel down. Sit between your heels and stop at the depth where your heels stay flat.
mistakes.cue: Heels flat; sit down between them.

mistakes.title: Knees caving in
mistakes.looksLike: As you sit down or stand up, your knees fall inward toward each other, inside the line of your feet.
mistakes.why: Your knees bend at an angle instead of straight over your feet, and your hips do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Push your knees out over your second toes. If they keep caving, use a lighter dumbbell or squat a little less deep.
mistakes.cue: Knees out over your toes.

safety: Start light. Use a dumbbell you can keep against your chest for every rep.
Pick the dumbbell up and set it down with bent knees, keeping it close to your body.
If your knees or back hurt, reduce the depth or the weight. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Bodyweight Squat
harder: Increase load gradually

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Standing tall, feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out, one dumbbell held vertically against the chest with both palms cupping its top end, elbows pointing down, eyes forward.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Hips at or just below knee height, heels flat, knees over the toes, torso fairly upright, dumbbell still vertical against the chest, elbows just inside the knees.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
summary: A wide-stance squat that puts more of the work on your inner thighs.
startingPosition: Feet about one and a half times shoulder-width apart, toes turned out about 30–45°. Hold one dumbbell vertically by its top end with both hands, arms long, so it hangs between your legs. Chest up, eyes forward.
steps: Set your feet wide, about one and a half times shoulder-width, toes turned out about 30–45°.
Hold one dumbbell by its top end with both hands so it hangs straight down between your legs.
Brace your trunk and let your arms hang long and relaxed.
Bend your hips and knees to sink straight down, with your knees tracking out over your toes.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, or as deep as you can control.
Stand up by pushing through your whole foot, keeping your knees out over your toes.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Sink straight down over two to three seconds, knees tracking out over your toes, dumbbell hanging still.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Push through your whole foot and stand tall in about one to two seconds, hips fully straight at the top.

breathing: Breathe in and brace before you lower. Breathe out as you push up through the hardest part.

formChecks.check: Each knee points the same way as its foot, over the second toe, at about 30–45° out from straight ahead.
The dumbbell hangs straight down between your feet and doesn't swing, and both feet stay flat.
Your torso stays more upright than in a regular squat, and your hips move mostly down rather than back.

mistakes.title: Knees falling inside the toes
mistakes.looksLike: Your toes point out at 30–45°, but your knees point straight ahead or inward, so they sit inside your feet.
mistakes.why: Your knees and feet end up pointing different ways, and your glutes and inner thighs do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Push your knees out so each one points over your second toe. If you can't, turn your toes in a little or narrow your stance.
mistakes.cue: Knees out, aimed at your second toes.

mistakes.title: Stance too wide
mistakes.looksLike: Your feet are so wide that you roll onto their inside edges and can only bend a few inches.
mistakes.why: You lose whole-foot contact, which makes you less steady, and the range gets too short to work your legs well.
mistakes.fix: Bring your feet in until both stay flat through the whole rep. About one and a half times shoulder-width is a good start.
mistakes.cue: Bring feet in until both stay flat.

mistakes.title: Chest falling forward
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips shoot back and your chest drops toward the floor, so the dumbbell swings out in front of your knees.
mistakes.why: The squat turns into a bend at the hips, so your lower back works more and your thighs work less.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest up and sit straight down between your heels. Keep your shoulders over the dumbbell so it hangs between your feet.
mistakes.cue: Shoulders stay over the dumbbell.

safety: Use a dumbbell you can hold with a firm grip for the whole set. If your grip gives out first, go lighter.
Stop each rep before the dumbbell touches the floor.
If your hips or knees hurt in the wide stance, narrow it and turn your toes out less. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Bodyweight Squat
harder: Pause for two seconds at the bottom

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Standing tall, feet about one and a half times shoulder-width, toes turned out about 30–45°, one dumbbell held vertically by its top end in both hands, arms long, hanging between the legs.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Thighs about parallel to the floor, knees pushed out over the toes, heels flat, torso upright, arms long, dumbbell hanging straight down between the feet a few inches above the floor.

name: Wall Sit
summary: A still hold against a wall that builds endurance in the front of your thighs.
startingPosition: Stand with your back flat against a clear wall, feet hip-width apart and about two foot-lengths out from it, toes forward. Arms crossed loosely or hanging at your sides, eyes forward.
steps: Stand with your back flat against the wall and walk your feet out about two foot-lengths, hip-width apart.
Slide your back down the wall until your knees bend to a height you can hold.
Adjust your feet so your knees sit directly above your ankles and your shins are vertical.
Keep your thighs parallel to the floor or higher, with your weight spread across your whole foot.
Hold for the target time, then slide back up the wall and walk your feet in.

phases.label: Slide down
phases.text: Slide down the wall over two to three seconds to the height you plan to hold.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Hold still for your target number of seconds, back on the wall, knees over ankles, breathing steadily.

phases.label: Slide up
phases.text: Press your back into the wall and slide up over two to three seconds before walking your feet in.

breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily through the whole hold. Don't hold your breath, even near the end.
cues: Press your feet into the floor.

formChecks.check: Your knees sit directly above your ankles, so your shins are vertical and your knees stay well behind your toes.
Your thighs are parallel to the floor or higher, so your hips are level with or above your knees.
Your hips and shoulder blades stay against the wall for the whole hold.

mistakes.title: Feet too close to the wall
mistakes.looksLike: Your feet are tucked in under you, so your knees push forward past your toes and your heels feel light.
mistakes.why: Your shins tilt forward, more of the load sits at the front of your knees, and the hold gets harder to balance.
mistakes.fix: Walk your feet out until your knees stack over your ankles and your shins are vertical at your chosen height.
mistakes.cue: Walk your feet out, shins vertical.

mistakes.title: Sitting too low
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips drop below your knees, so your thighs slope down toward the wall.
mistakes.why: Below parallel the hold gets much harder to keep still, and it goes deeper than this exercise needs.
mistakes.fix: Slide up until your thighs are parallel to the floor or higher. Beginners start higher and lower a little over the weeks.
mistakes.cue: Slide up, hips no lower than knees.

mistakes.title: Back peeling off the wall
mistakes.looksLike: Your shoulders round forward off the wall, or you lean forward and push your hands into your thighs.
mistakes.why: Your arms take part of the load off your legs, and the vertical-shin position is lost.
mistakes.fix: Press your hips and shoulder blades into the wall. Cross your arms or let them hang so your hands don't push on your thighs.
mistakes.cue: Shoulders on the wall, hands off legs.

safety: Use a non-slip floor and shoes with grip, or bare feet, so your feet can't slide out.
If your knees hurt, slide higher up the wall to bend them less. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
Start with holds you can finish in good position, and add a few seconds at a time.
easier: Sit higher on the wall with less knee bend
harder: Hold longer with thighs parallel to the floor

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing with back flat against a wall, feet hip-width apart and about two foot-lengths out from the wall, toes forward, arms relaxed at the sides.

frames.label: Hold
frames.pose: Back flat against the wall, thighs parallel to the floor, knees bent 90° directly above the ankles, shins vertical, feet flat, arms crossed loosely at the chest.

name: Split Squat
summary: A staggered-stance squat that trains one leg at a time with both feet down.
equipment: none (wall or chair for balance optional)
startingPosition: Long staggered stance: front foot flat, back foot about a stride behind on the ball of the foot. Feet hip-width apart side to side, like train tracks. Hips facing forward, torso tall, eyes forward.
steps: Step one foot back about a stride's length and rise onto the ball of that back foot.
Set your feet hip-width apart side to side, like train tracks, with your hips facing forward.
Lower straight down by bending both knees, so your back knee moves toward the floor under your hip.
Stop just above the floor, or as low as you can control, with your front heel flat.
Push through your whole front foot to rise, keeping both feet planted for every rep.
Finish all reps on one side, then switch legs.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Drop your back knee straight toward the floor over two to three seconds, torso upright or leaning slightly forward.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Push through your whole front foot and rise in about one to two seconds, with both feet staying where they are.

breathing: Breathe in and brace at the top. Breathe out as you push back up through your front foot.
cues: Back knee straight down under your hip.
Push the floor away with your front foot.

formChecks.check: At the bottom, your back knee is under your hip, a few inches off the floor, and your front heel is flat.
Your torso stays upright or leans slightly forward, with no bend at the waist.
Your feet stay hip-width apart like train tracks, your front knee stays over your front foot and your hips stay level.

mistakes.title: Feet on a tightrope
mistakes.looksLike: Your back foot lines up directly behind your front foot, and you wobble or your hips twist to one side.
mistakes.why: A narrow base gives you little side-to-side balance, so you spend the set steadying yourself instead of using your legs.
mistakes.fix: Set your feet hip-width apart side to side, like train tracks. Hold a wall or chair lightly if you still wobble.
mistakes.cue: Feet hip-width apart, side to side.

mistakes.title: Front heel lifting
mistakes.looksLike: As you lower, your weight drifts forward, your front knee shoots ahead and your front heel peels off the floor.
mistakes.why: Your weight moves onto the ball of the front foot, balance gets shaky, and your glutes do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Lengthen your stance and lower your back knee straight down under your hip. Keep your front heel heavy the whole rep.
mistakes.cue: Longer stance, front heel planted.

mistakes.title: Folding at the waist
mistakes.looksLike: Your chest drops toward your front thigh, well past a slight forward lean, and your hips push back as you lower.
mistakes.why: The work shifts from your front leg toward your hips and lower back, and your balance gets harder to hold.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest tall over your hips and lower your back knee straight down. A slight forward lean is fine.
mistakes.cue: Chest stays tall over your hips.

safety: Hold a wall or chair lightly with one hand if you wobble. It's a fine way to learn.
If your front knee hurts, lengthen your stance or lower only partway. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
Put a folded towel under your back knee if it touches the floor.
easier: Hold a wall or chair and lower only partway
harder: Reverse Lunge

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Long staggered stance, front foot flat, back foot a stride behind on the ball of the foot, both legs nearly straight, torso tall, hands on hips, eyes forward.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Both knees bent about 90°, back knee a few inches above the floor directly under the hip, front knee over the front foot, front heel flat, torso upright, hands on hips.

name: Reverse Lunge
summary: A backward step into a lunge that trains each leg and your balance.
startingPosition: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, toes forward, weight spread across both feet. Hands on your hips or arms relaxed at your sides, eyes forward. Check there's clear space behind you.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and brace your trunk.
Step one foot back about a stride's length, landing on the ball of the foot, still hip-width from the front foot.
Lower your back knee toward the floor under your hip, keeping your front heel flat.
Stop just above the floor, or as low as you can control.
Push through your whole front foot to bring the back foot forward and stand tall.
Alternate legs, or finish all reps on one side before switching.

phases.label: Step and lower
phases.text: Step back and lower over two to three seconds, back knee dropping toward the floor under your hip.

phases.label: Return
phases.text: Push through your front foot and bring your back foot forward to stand tall in about one to two seconds.

breathing: Breathe in as you step back and lower. Breathe out as you push through your front foot to stand.
cues: Step back on train tracks, not a tightrope.
Back knee down under your hip.
Stand up through the front foot.
Stand all the way tall between reps.

formChecks.check: At the bottom, your back knee is under your hip, a few inches off the floor, and your front heel is flat.
Your back foot lands hip-width from your front foot, not behind it, and your front knee stays over your front foot.
Your torso stays upright or leans slightly forward, and you stand fully tall between reps.

mistakes.title: Stepping onto a tightrope
mistakes.looksLike: Your back foot lands right behind or across from your front foot, and you wobble or your hips twist.
mistakes.why: A narrow base leaves you little side-to-side balance, so steadying yourself takes over from the leg work.
mistakes.fix: Step straight back on train tracks, hip-width apart. Fix your eyes on a point ahead, and hold a wall lightly if you need to.
mistakes.cue: Step straight back, feet hip-width.

mistakes.title: Step too short
mistakes.looksLike: Your back foot lands close behind you, so your front knee shoots forward and your front heel lifts as you lower.
mistakes.why: Your weight moves onto the ball of the front foot, balance gets harder, and your glutes do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Step back far enough that your back knee can drop straight down under your hip while your front heel stays flat.
mistakes.cue: Step farther back, front heel flat.

mistakes.title: Pushing off the back foot
mistakes.looksLike: To get back up, you shove hard off your back toes and the front leg only straightens at the very end.
mistakes.why: The back leg does the work meant for the front leg, so the front leg gets less training.
mistakes.fix: Drive through your front heel and midfoot to stand, and let the back foot follow lightly. Slow the return if you need to.
mistakes.cue: Drive up through your front heel.

safety: Hold a wall or chair with one hand if your balance is shaky.
If your front knee hurts, take a longer step or lower only partway. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
Clear the space behind you before you start, and step back only as far as you can control.
easier: Split Squat
harder: Bulgarian Split Squat

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing tall, feet hip-width apart, toes forward, hands on hips, eyes forward.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: One foot stepped back a stride, on the ball of the foot, back knee a few inches above the floor under the hip, front knee bent about 90° over the front foot, front heel flat, torso upright, hands on hips.

name: Step-Up
summary: A step onto a raised surface that trains one leg to lift and lower your body.
equipment: sturdy step, box or the bottom stair
startingPosition: Stand facing a sturdy step, box or the bottom stair. Put one whole foot on top, heel included, knee over the foot. Other foot flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Torso tall, hands on hips or on a rail.
steps: Place your whole foot on the step, heel included, with your knee pointing over your toes.
Lean your torso slightly forward so your weight moves over the top foot.
Drive through the top foot to stand tall on the step, pushing as little as you can with the bottom foot.
Bring your other foot up so you stand on the step with both feet.
Step the trailing foot back down slowly, letting the top leg control the lowering.
Finish all reps on one leg, then switch.

phases.label: Step up
phases.text: Drive through your top foot and stand tall on the step in about one to two seconds.

phases.label: Step down
phases.text: Lower the trailing foot to the floor over two to three seconds, with the top leg doing the work.

breathing: Breathe in before you step up and breathe out as you drive up. Breathe in again as you lower.
cues: Weight over the top foot first.
Bottom foot just along for the ride.

formChecks.check: Your whole top foot is on the step, heel included, and it stays there for every rep.
Your top knee stays in line with your second toe as you rise and as you lower.
The trailing foot touches down softly, with no bounce off the floor to start the next rep.

mistakes.title: Pushing off the bottom foot
mistakes.looksLike: You bounce or spring off your back toes to get up, and the top leg only straightens near the end.
mistakes.why: The bottom leg does much of the lifting, so the top leg gets less of the work the exercise is meant to train.
mistakes.fix: Shift your weight over the top foot first, then stand up through it. Lift the toes of your bottom foot so they can't push.
mistakes.cue: Shift onto the top foot, then stand.

mistakes.title: Only the toes on the step
mistakes.looksLike: Your heel hangs off the edge of the step, so you balance on the ball of your top foot.
mistakes.why: Your base is smaller, balance gets harder, and the work shifts toward the front of your knee and away from your glutes.
mistakes.fix: Place your whole foot on the step, heel included. If the step is too shallow, find a deeper one.
mistakes.cue: Heel on the step, whole foot down.

mistakes.title: Knee caving inward
mistakes.looksLike: As you rise onto the step, your top knee falls inward, inside the line of your foot.
mistakes.why: Your knee bends at an angle instead of straight over your foot, and your hip muscles do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Keep your top knee over your second toe as you rise and as you lower. Use a lower step until you can.
mistakes.cue: Knee over your second toe.

safety: Use a step, box or stair that's stable and won't slide. Stand near a rail or wall you can hold.
Start low, around the height of the bottom stair, and go higher only when every rep is controlled.
If your knee hurts, use a lower step. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Use a lower step and hold a rail
harder: Use a higher step, up to knee height

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Facing a sturdy box about mid-shin height, one whole foot flat on top with the knee bent over it, other foot flat on the floor behind, torso leaning slightly forward, hands on hips.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Standing tall on top of the box on both feet, hips and knees straight, hands on hips, eyes forward.

name: Lateral Lunge
summary: A side step into a one-leg squat that trains your legs and inner thighs.
startingPosition: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, toes forward, hands clasped at your chest or on your hips, eyes forward. Check there's clear space to your side.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and brace your trunk.
Take a wide step out to one side, landing with your foot flat and toes pointing forward or slightly out.
Sit your hips back and down over the stepping leg, keeping the other leg straight with its foot flat.
Lower until the bent knee is over your foot, or as far as you can control with both feet flat.
Push through the whole foot of the bent leg to return to standing, then repeat or switch sides.

phases.label: Step and sit
phases.text: Step out and sit your hips back over the bent leg over two to three seconds, other leg straight.

phases.label: Return
phases.text: Push through the whole foot of the bent leg to come back to standing in about one to two seconds.

breathing: Breathe in as you step out and sit back. Breathe out as you push back to standing.
cues: Hips back, not just knee forward.
Both feet flat, toes forward or slightly out.
Push the floor away to come back.

formChecks.check: The bent knee stays over the second toe of that foot, and the other leg stays straight.
Both feet stay flat, pointing forward or slightly out, with no rolling onto the edge of the straight leg's foot.
Your hips sit back behind the heel of the bent leg and your chest leans slightly forward, with that heel flat.

mistakes.title: Not sitting back into the hip
mistakes.looksLike: Your torso stays straight up and down and your knee pushes far forward, so the heel of the bent leg starts to lift.
mistakes.why: The front of your thigh does nearly all the work, your glutes do little, and the lifting heel makes you unsteady.
mistakes.fix: Push your hips back as you bend, as if sitting onto a chair behind you, with your chest leaning slightly forward and heel down.
mistakes.cue: Sit your hips back toward a chair.

mistakes.title: Bending the straight leg
mistakes.looksLike: The leg you stepped away from bends at the knee, so you end up in a half squat on both legs.
mistakes.why: Your weight splits between both legs, so the working leg does less and the straight leg's inner thigh barely lengthens.
mistakes.fix: Keep the other leg straight with its foot flat. Lower only as far as you can while it stays straight.
mistakes.cue: Other leg straight, foot flat.

mistakes.title: Knee collapsing inward
mistakes.looksLike: The bent knee drifts inside the line of your foot and that foot rolls onto its inner edge.
mistakes.why: Your knee moves out of line with your hip and foot, and your glutes do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Point the bent knee over your second toe and keep big toe, little toe and heel down. Turning the toes out slightly can help.
mistakes.cue: Bent knee over your second toe.

safety: Step only as wide as you can control. Hold a wall or chair for balance while you learn.
If your knee or inner thigh hurts, take a shorter step and lower less. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Take a shorter step and lower only partway
harder: Pause for two seconds at the bottom

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing tall, feet hip-width apart, toes forward, hands clasped at the chest, eyes forward.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Wide stance, right knee bent over the right foot with hips pushed back, left leg straight, both feet flat and pointing forward, torso leaning slightly forward, hands clasped at the chest.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
summary: A split squat with the back foot raised, putting more work on the front leg.
equipment: bench or sturdy chair behind you
startingPosition: Face away from a bench or sturdy chair, front foot flat about a long stride in front of it, laces of the back foot resting on the seat. Feet hip-width apart side to side, hips facing forward, torso tall.
steps: Stand facing away from a bench or sturdy chair, with your front foot about a long stride in front of it.
Rest the laces of your back foot on the seat, feet hip-width apart side to side.
Shift most of your weight onto your front leg and brace your trunk.
Lower your back knee toward the floor under your hip, front heel flat, torso upright or leaning slightly forward.
Push through your whole front foot to rise, with the back foot resting lightly.
Finish all reps on one leg, then switch.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower over two to three seconds, back knee dropping straight toward the floor under your hip, front heel flat.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Push through your front foot and stand in about one to two seconds, rear foot resting lightly on the bench.

breathing: Breathe in and brace at the top. Breathe out as you push up through your front foot.
cues: Back foot rests, it doesn't push.

formChecks.check: At the bottom, your front heel is flat, your front knee is roughly over your front foot and your back knee is under your hip.
Your torso is upright or leaning slightly forward, with no bend at the waist and no lean back toward the bench.
Your feet stay hip-width apart, your front knee stays over your second toe and your hips stay level.

mistakes.title: Front foot too close to the bench
mistakes.looksLike: Your front foot sits close to the bench, so your front knee shoots forward and your front heel lifts as you lower.
mistakes.why: Your weight rolls onto the ball of your front foot, which cramps the position and makes balance hard.
mistakes.fix: Move your front foot out to about a long stride from the bench, so your front heel stays flat at the bottom.
mistakes.cue: Front foot out a long stride.

mistakes.title: Pushing with the back leg
mistakes.looksLike: You press down into the bench with your back foot to rise, and your hips drift back toward the bench.
mistakes.why: The back leg takes over part of the lift, so the front leg gets less of the work the exercise is meant for.
mistakes.fix: Keep most of your weight on your front foot. Rest the back laces lightly, as if you could lift that foot at any time.
mistakes.cue: Most weight on the front foot.

mistakes.title: Feet on a tightrope
mistakes.looksLike: Your front foot lines up directly in front of your back foot, and your hips twist or sway as you lower.
mistakes.why: A narrow base gives you little side-to-side balance, so you spend the set steadying yourself instead of using your leg.
mistakes.fix: Set your feet hip-width apart side to side, like train tracks. Hold a wall or rail lightly if you still wobble.
mistakes.cue: Feet on train tracks, hip-width apart.

safety: Use a bench or chair that can't slide, about knee height or lower. Set a chair against a wall.
Hold a wall or rail with one hand if you wobble. It's a fine way to learn the position.
If your front knee or the front of your back hip hurts, use a lower seat or a regular split squat. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Split Squat
harder: Pause for two seconds at the bottom

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Facing away from a bench, front foot flat a long stride ahead of it, laces of the back foot resting on the bench, front leg nearly straight, torso tall, hands on hips.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Front knee bent about 90° over the front foot, front heel flat, back knee bent and a few inches above the floor under the hip, back laces on the bench, torso leaning slightly forward, hands on hips.

name: Hip Hinge
summary: Teaches you to bend from your hips with a long back, the base of every hinge.
startingPosition: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, knees softly bent. Rest your hands on your hips, or hold a dowel along your spine so it touches your head, upper back and tailbone. Eyes forward.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, hands on your hips or a dowel held along your back.
Push your hips straight back, as if reaching them toward a wall behind you, and let your chest tip forward.
Keep your shins close to vertical and your back long, with the dowel touching your head, upper back and tailbone.
Stop when your hips can't travel farther back or you feel a strong stretch in the backs of your thighs.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, glutes squeezed and ribs stacked over your hips.

phases.label: Hinging
phases.text: Push your hips back over two to three seconds while your chest tips forward and your shins stay nearly vertical.

phases.label: Standing
phases.text: Drive your hips forward over about one second and finish tall, ribs over hips, without leaning back.

breathing: Breathe in and brace lightly before you hinge. Breathe out as you drive your hips forward to stand.
cues: Imagine closing a car door with your hips.
Dowel touches head, upper back and tailbone.

formChecks.check: At the bottom, your shins are nearly vertical, your hips sit well behind your heels and your chest has tipped forward rather than dropped straight down.
The dowel stays touching your head, upper back and tailbone the whole rep, with a small gap at your lower back.
At the top, your shoulders, hips and ankles stack in one vertical line, not with your shoulders behind your hips.

mistakes.title: Bending mostly at the knees
mistakes.looksLike: Your knees bend a lot and push forward, your shins tilt toward your toes, and your hips drop down instead of moving back.
mistakes.why: The work shifts to the front of your thighs, and you miss the hip movement this drill is meant to teach.
mistakes.fix: Keep your shins nearly vertical. Stand a foot in front of a wall and push your hips back to tap it, then move a little farther away.
mistakes.cue: Shins upright, hips back to the wall.

mistakes.title: Rounding the back
mistakes.looksLike: Your upper back curls and your head drops, or your lower back rounds near the bottom. With a dowel, it lifts off your head or tailbone.
mistakes.why: The bend comes from your spine instead of your hips, so your glutes and hamstrings do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Keep all three dowel contact points for the whole rep. End the rep as soon as one lifts off, even if that range feels short.
mistakes.cue: Back flat; stop before it rounds.

mistakes.title: Leaning back at the top
mistakes.looksLike: Standing up at the end of the rep but leaning backward: your hips push forward past your feet, your shoulders end up behind your hips and your lower back arches.
mistakes.why: The rep is done once you stand straight. Leaning past that moves the effort from your glutes to your lower back.
mistakes.fix: Finish with a firm glute squeeze and your ribs stacked over your hips. Think "stand tall", not "lean back".
mistakes.cue: Ribs over hips, glutes squeezed.

safety: Work in a range you can control without pain. A short hinge with a long back is better than a deep one with a rounded back.
If your lower back feels pinched or strained, shorten the range or swap to the glute bridge for that session. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Glute Bridge
harder: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing tall, feet hip-width apart, knees softly bent, hands resting on the hips, chest up, eyes forward.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Hands still on the hips. Hips pushed far back behind the heels, shins nearly vertical, knees softly bent, torso tipped forward about 45° with a flat back from head to tailbone.

name: Glute Bridge
summary: Trains your glutes to straighten your hips while your back stays still.
startingPosition: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, heels about a foot from your glutes. Arms rest by your sides, palms down. Ribs down, lower back relaxed on the floor, chin gently tucked.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, heels about a foot from your glutes.
Breathe out to bring your ribs down and lightly brace your stomach.
Press through your whole foot, heels heavy, to lift your hips off the floor.
Stop when your knees, hips and shoulders form a straight line, and squeeze your glutes for a breath.
Lower your hips to the floor with control and reset before the next rep.

phases.label: Lifting
phases.text: Press through your heels to raise your hips over about one second until knees, hips and shoulders line up.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Pause for one to two seconds at the top with your glutes squeezed and ribs down.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower your hips to the floor over two seconds, touching down lightly.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift your hips and hold the top. Breathe in as you lower to the floor.
cues: Squeeze your glutes, not your lower back.
Straight line knees to shoulders, no higher.

formChecks.check: At the top, your knees, hips and shoulders form one straight line, and your shins are close to vertical.
Your ribs stay down and your hips stop at the line, with no upward curve in your lower back.
Your knees stay hip-width apart and point straight over your feet, rather than falling in or flaring out.

mistakes.title: Over-arching the lower back
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips rise above the line from knees to shoulders, your ribs flare up and your lower back arches into a curve.
mistakes.why: The extra height comes from bending your lower back, not straightening your hips, so your glutes do less of the lift.
mistakes.fix: Breathe out and pull your ribs down before you lift. Stop at a straight line from knees to shoulders and squeeze your glutes there.
mistakes.cue: Ribs down; stop at a straight line.

mistakes.title: Pushing through the toes
mistakes.looksLike: Your heels peel off the floor at the top and your weight rolls onto the balls of your feet, often because your feet are too close.
mistakes.why: Pressing through your toes shifts work to the front of your thighs and calves and away from your glutes.
mistakes.fix: Keep your whole foot down and think "heels heavy". If it helps, lift your toes slightly off the floor for a few reps.
mistakes.cue: Heels pressed down, whole foot flat.

mistakes.title: Feet too far away
mistakes.looksLike: Your heels sit far from your hips, your shins slant away from you at the top, and the backs of your thighs cramp or take over.
mistakes.why: With your feet that far out, your hamstrings do most of the lifting and your glutes do less.
mistakes.fix: Walk your heels in until your shins are close to vertical at the top. If a hamstring cramps, stop, shake it out and reset.
mistakes.cue: Walk heels in; shins upright at top.

safety: If your lower back aches, lift less high and focus on keeping your ribs down. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
Use a mat or a folded towel under your upper back and head if the floor feels hard.
easier: Lift partway and build height over a few sessions
harder: Hip Thrust

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Lying on the back on a mat, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart about a foot from the glutes, arms by the sides with palms down, lower back relaxed on the mat.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Hips lifted so knees, hips and shoulders form a straight line, shins near vertical, whole foot flat, upper back and arms on the mat, ribs down, no arch in the lower back.

name: Hip Thrust
summary: Trains your glutes through a bigger range than the floor bridge.
equipment: a sturdy couch edge or bench
startingPosition: Sit on the floor, the bottom edge of your shoulder blades against the edge of a sturdy couch or bench. Knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart about a foot in front of your hips, elbows on the bench, chin tucked.
steps: Sit on the floor with the bottom edge of your shoulder blades against the edge of a sturdy couch or bench.
Set your feet flat and hip-width apart, about a foot in front of your hips, so your shins will be vertical at the top.
Tuck your chin, bring your ribs down and press through your heels to lift your hips.
Pivot on your shoulder blades until your knees, hips and shoulders form a straight line, eyes looking forward.
Squeeze your glutes for a breath, then lower your hips toward the floor with control.

phases.label: Lifting
phases.text: Press through your heels and pivot on the bench edge to raise your hips over about one second.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Pause for one to two seconds at the top: chin tucked, eyes forward, ribs down, glutes squeezed.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower your hips over two seconds until they hover just above the floor.

breathing: Breathe in and brace at the bottom. Breathe out as you lift and hold the top, then breathe in as you lower.

formChecks.check: At the top, your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, with knees, hips and shoulders in a straight line and shins close to vertical.
Your chin stays tucked so your eyes look forward toward your knees, not up at the ceiling.
Your knees stay hip-width apart over your feet, and both hips rise to the same height.

mistakes.title: Arching to finish the rep
mistakes.looksLike: At the top your head tips back, your ribs flare and your lower back curves, so your hips rise above the line from knees to shoulders.
mistakes.why: The last bit of height comes from your lower back instead of your hips, so your glutes stop doing the work at the top.
mistakes.fix: Tuck your chin, keep your eyes forward and bring your ribs down. Stop at a straight line from knees to shoulders and squeeze your glutes.
mistakes.cue: Chin tucked; stop at a straight line.

mistakes.title: Bench too high or low on your back
mistakes.looksLike: The edge sits up at your neck or down near your waist, so you slide along it or fold around it as your hips rise.
mistakes.why: Without a steady pivot point at your shoulder blades, your torso can't move as one piece and the rep is harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Set the edge just below your shoulder blades and rest your elbows on top. Keep that same contact point for every rep.
mistakes.cue: Bench edge just below shoulder blades.

mistakes.title: Shins slanting at the top
mistakes.looksLike: At the top your knees sit well in front of or well behind your ankles, so your shins slant clearly away from vertical.
mistakes.why: Feet too close shifts work to the front of your thighs; too far shifts it to your hamstrings. Either way your glutes do less.
mistakes.fix: Do one rep and hold the top. Move your feet until your shins are close to vertical, then keep that spot for the set.
mistakes.cue: Adjust feet until shins are upright.

safety: Set the bench or couch against a wall so it can't slide, and test that it stays put before your first rep.
If the edge digs into your back, pad it with a folded towel. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
If your lower back aches, lift less high and focus on ribs down, or go back to the glute bridge.
easier: Glute Bridge
harder: Hold the top for three seconds on each rep

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Seated on a mat, lower edge of the shoulder blades on the edge of a bench, hips just above the floor, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, elbows resting on the bench.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Shoulder blades pivoted on the bench edge, hips lifted so knees, hips and shoulders form a straight line parallel to the floor, shins vertical, chin tucked, head in line with the torso.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
summary: Trains each glute on its own while you keep your hips level.
startingPosition: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, heels about a foot from your glutes. Lift one foot and straighten that leg so your thighs stay level. Arms by your sides, palms down, ribs down.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, heels about a foot from your glutes.
Lift one foot and straighten that leg so both thighs stay side by side.
Bring your ribs down and press through the heel of your planted foot to lift your hips.
Rise until the working knee, hips and shoulders line up, keeping both hips at the same height.
Lower with control, finish all reps on that side, then switch legs.

phases.label: Lifting
phases.text: Press through your planted heel to lift your hips over about one second, both sides rising together.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Pause for one to two seconds at the top with your hips level and the working glute squeezed.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower over two seconds and touch down lightly before the next rep.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift and hold the top. Breathe in as you lower.
cues: Ribs down, stop at a straight line.

formChecks.check: Filmed from your feet, your belt line stays level at the top and the side of your lifted leg does not drop.
At the top, the working knee, hips and shoulders make a straight line and the working shin is close to vertical.
Your working knee points straight over your foot and doesn't drift in or out as you lift.

mistakes.title: Hip dropping on the free-leg side
mistakes.looksLike: At the top, the hip on the side of your lifted leg sits lower than the other, so your belt line tilts toward the floor.
mistakes.why: The muscles on the side of your working hip should hold your pelvis level. When it tilts, they and your glute do less.
mistakes.fix: Lift only as high as you can with level hips. Rest your hands on your hip bones for a few reps to feel them stay even.
mistakes.cue: Hips level; lift only that high.

mistakes.title: Arching to get higher
mistakes.looksLike: Your ribs flare, your lower back arches and your hips rise above the line from your working knee to your shoulders.
mistakes.why: The extra height comes from your spine, not your hip, so the working glute does less of the lift.
mistakes.fix: Bring your ribs down before each rep and stop at a straight line. If it keeps happening, hug your free knee to your chest.
mistakes.cue: Stop at a straight line, not higher.

mistakes.title: Working foot too far away
mistakes.looksLike: Your planted heel sits far from your hips, the working shin slants away from you at the top, and the back of that thigh cramps.
mistakes.why: With the foot that far out, your hamstring takes over the lift and your glute does less.
mistakes.fix: Bring your heel in until the working shin is close to vertical at the top. If it cramps, stop, shake it out and reset.
mistakes.cue: Heel in until your shin is upright.

safety: If you can't keep your hips level, do fewer reps, or go back to the two-leg bridge for a few sessions.
If your lower back or hamstring feels strained, lift less high and reset your foot. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Glute Bridge
harder: Pause for three seconds at the top of each rep

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Lying on the back on a mat, one knee bent with the foot flat about a foot from the glutes, the other leg straight and lifted so both thighs are level, arms by the sides, palms down.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Hips lifted on one planted foot so working knee, hips and shoulders form a straight line, working shin near vertical, free leg straight in line with that thigh, upper back on the mat.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
summary: A loaded hip hinge that trains your glutes and hamstrings from the top down.
startingPosition: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand against the front of your thighs, palms facing you. Knees softly bent, shoulders down and back, ribs stacked over hips, eyes forward.
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand against the front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart, knees softly bent.
Keep that small knee bend fixed and push your hips back, sliding the dumbbells down the front of your legs.
Keep the weights brushing your legs and your back long as your chest tips forward.
Stop when your hips stop moving back or you feel a strong hamstring stretch, often between the knee and mid-shin.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, glutes squeezed, without leaning back at the top.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Push your hips back and slide the dumbbells down your legs over two to three seconds, knees holding their slight bend.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Drive your hips forward over about one second, keeping the dumbbells close, and finish standing tall.

breathing: Breathe in and brace before you push your hips back. Hold the brace on the way down and breathe out as you stand tall.
cues: Drag the dumbbells down your legs.
Long back from head to tailbone.

formChecks.check: The dumbbells stay against or within a finger's width of your legs and travel in a straight vertical line over your mid-foot.
Your knee angle stays the same from top to bottom, with your shins close to vertical while your hips move back.
At the bottom, your back is flat from head to tailbone and the dumbbells sit around the knees to mid-shin, not near the floor.

mistakes.title: Weights drifting away from the legs
mistakes.looksLike: On the way down the dumbbells swing forward and hang out over your toes, with a clear gap between the weights and your legs.
mistakes.why: The farther the load sits from your hips, the more your back has to hold it, and the less your glutes and hamstrings drive the lift.
mistakes.fix: Draw your shoulders down and back to keep the weights against your thighs. Slide them down the front of your legs like they're on rails.
mistakes.cue: Shoulders back, weights on your legs.

mistakes.title: Bending the knees as you lower
mistakes.looksLike: As you go down your knees bend more and push forward, your hips sink and your shins tilt toward your toes, like a squat.
mistakes.why: The front of your thighs takes over, and the hamstring stretch that makes this exercise work fades.
mistakes.fix: Set a slight knee bend at the top and hold that exact angle. Think hips back toward the wall behind you, not down toward the floor.
mistakes.cue: Knees keep the same slight bend.

mistakes.title: Chasing the floor
mistakes.looksLike: You keep lowering after your hips stop moving back, so your back rounds and the dumbbells head toward your feet.
mistakes.why: Past that point your spine bends instead of your hips, so the load moves off your glutes and hamstrings and onto your back.
mistakes.fix: End each rep where your hips stop moving back, usually around the knee to mid-shin for beginners. Your range can grow with practice.
mistakes.cue: Rise as soon as your hips stop moving.

mistakes.title: Leaning back at the top
mistakes.looksLike: At the finish you push your hips past your feet and your shoulders end up behind your hips, arching your lower back.
mistakes.why: The rep is done once you stand straight. Leaning past that adds nothing for your glutes and loads your lower back.
mistakes.fix: Finish with a firm glute squeeze and your ribs stacked over your hips. Stand tall, then start the next rep.
mistakes.cue: Squeeze glutes, ribs over hips.

safety: Choose a load you can lower under control for every rep. Add weight in small steps only when all reps look the same.
Pick the dumbbells up from a raised surface or with a deadlift, so you don't start the set bent over and rounded.
If your lower back feels strained, shorten the range or go lighter. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Hip Hinge
harder: Add a little load once every rep looks the same

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Standing tall, feet hip-width apart, knees softly bent, a dumbbell in each hand resting against the front of the thighs, palms facing the body, shoulders stacked over hips.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Hips pushed back, knee bend unchanged, shins near vertical, flat back tipped forward, dumbbells against the legs just below the knees, arms hanging straight, neck in line with the back.

name: Dumbbell Deadlift
summary: Trains lifting a load from the floor with your legs and hips working together.
startingPosition: Feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell beside each foot, handles in line with your ankles. Grip them palms in, arms straight, hips between shoulder and knee height, back long, eyes on the floor a little ahead.
steps: Stand with a dumbbell beside each foot, handles in line with your ankles, or raised on sturdy blocks if you can't reach with a long back.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to grip the handles, palms facing in and arms straight.
Set your hips between your shoulders and knees, brace, and draw your shoulders down until the dumbbells feel tight in your hands.
Push the floor away so your hips and shoulders rise together until you stand tall.
Lower by pushing your hips back first, bend your knees once the weights pass them, and set the dumbbells down beside your feet.

phases.label: Lifting
phases.text: Push the floor away over one to two seconds, hips and shoulders rising together, dumbbells close to your legs.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Push your hips back, then bend your knees, setting the dumbbells down beside your feet over about two seconds.

phases.label: Reset
phases.text: Pause for about one second with the weights on the floor, then brace and set your back again before the next rep.

breathing: Breathe in and brace at the bottom before each rep. Breathe out at the top or as you set the weights down.
cues: Arms are long ropes; legs do the work.

formChecks.check: At the start, your hips sit higher than your knees and lower than your shoulders, with your knees clearly bent, unlike the RDL.
Your back angle stays the same as the weights leave the floor; hips and shoulders rise together until the dumbbells pass your knees.
At the top, your shoulders, hips and ankles stack in one vertical line, without leaning back.
The dumbbells travel straight up and down beside your feet, and your knees stay in line with your toes.

mistakes.title: Hips shooting up first
mistakes.looksLike: As the weights leave the floor your hips rise but your shoulders don't, so your knees straighten and your back tips toward horizontal.
mistakes.why: Your legs stop helping and it turns into a stiff-legged pull, with more of the load on your back and hamstrings.
mistakes.fix: Push the floor away so hips and shoulders rise at the same rate. Unlike the RDL, your knees bend here and do real work.
mistakes.cue: Legs push; shoulders rise with hips.

mistakes.title: Rounding to reach the floor
mistakes.looksLike: To grab the dumbbells your back curves and your shoulders roll forward, and your back stays rounded as you lift.
mistakes.why: Your spine bends instead of your hips and knees, so your legs and glutes do less and the lift is harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Raise the dumbbells on sturdy blocks or steps until you can grip them with a long back. Lower the blocks as your range improves.
mistakes.cue: Start from blocks with a long back.

mistakes.title: Yanking the weights off the floor
mistakes.looksLike: The dumbbells jerk off the floor, your elbows bend, and your back position changes in the first few inches of the lift.
mistakes.why: A jerk lets your back position slip before your legs take the load, so the hardest part of the lift is out of control.
mistakes.fix: Draw your shoulders down until the dumbbells feel tight, brace, then push the floor away smoothly with straight arms.
mistakes.cue: Arms straight, brace, push smoothly.

safety: Raise the dumbbells on sturdy blocks or steps if you can't reach them with a long back. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
Choose a load you can lift with the same back position on every rep, and add weight in small steps.
Set the weights down under control rather than dropping them, with clear space around your feet.
easier: Hip Hinge
harder: Add load in small steps once every rep looks the same

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Feet hip-width apart, dumbbells on the floor beside the feet, knees bent, hips between knee and shoulder height, flat back tipped forward, arms straight gripping the handles, neck in line.

frames.label: Lockout
frames.pose: Standing tall, knees and hips straight, shoulders stacked over hips over ankles, a dumbbell in each hand hanging at the sides beside the thighs, arms straight, palms facing in.

name: Band Pull-Through
summary: Trains your glutes to drive your hips forward against a band.
equipment: resistance band anchored low behind you
startingPosition: Anchor a band near ankle height to something sturdy. Face away from it, holding the band in both hands between your legs. Walk out until it's taut, feet a bit wider than hip-width, knees soft, arms long, eyes forward.
steps: Anchor a band low behind you, face away from it, and hold it with both hands between your legs.
Walk forward until the band is taut, with feet a little wider than hip-width and knees soft.
Push your hips back and let the band draw your hands back between your legs, back long and shins near vertical.
Snap your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes, arms straight and relaxed.
Pause tall for a beat, then hinge back under control for the next rep.

phases.label: Hinging
phases.text: Let the band draw your hips back over about two seconds while your chest tips forward and your back stays long.

phases.label: Hip snap
phases.text: Drive your hips forward in about one second to stand tall, arms hanging like hooks.

phases.label: Lockout
phases.text: Hold for about one second standing tall, glutes squeezed and ribs over hips.

breathing: Breathe in as the band draws your hips back. Breathe out as you snap your hips forward to stand.
cues: Hips back, then snap them through.
Long back on the way down.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.

formChecks.check: Your arms stay straight and hang from your shoulders; your hands move only because your hips move.
At the bottom, your hips sit well behind your heels, with shins near vertical and a flat back.
At the top, your shoulders, hips and ankles line up vertically, without your shoulders falling behind your hips.

mistakes.title: Pulling with the arms
mistakes.looksLike: Your elbows bend and your hands yank the band forward to your hips, while your hips barely move.
mistakes.why: Your arms take over a job meant for your hips, so your glutes and hamstrings do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Keep your arms long and loose. Treat your hands as hooks and move the band only by driving your hips forward.
mistakes.cue: Arms long; hips move the band.

mistakes.title: Squatting instead of hinging
mistakes.looksLike: Your knees bend and push forward, your hips sink down and your torso stays upright, so your hips barely move back.
mistakes.why: It turns into a squat, so the front of your thighs works and your glutes and hamstrings do less.
mistakes.fix: Keep your shins close to vertical and reach your hips back toward the anchor until you feel the backs of your thighs stretch.
mistakes.cue: Shins upright, hips reach back.

mistakes.title: Leaning back at the top
mistakes.looksLike: You drive past standing and arch your lower back, so your shoulders end up behind your hips.
mistakes.why: The hip snap is done once you're upright. Arching past that moves effort from your glutes to your lower back.
mistakes.fix: Finish tall with your ribs stacked over your hips and a firm glute squeeze. Stand straight, then hinge back.
mistakes.cue: Ribs stacked over hips at the finish.

safety: Use a fixed anchor that can't move, and check the band for nicks or tears before each session.
If the band pulls you off balance, step closer to the anchor or use a lighter band.
If your lower back feels strained, shorten the hinge. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Hip Hinge
harder: Use a heavier band or step farther from the anchor

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Standing tall facing away from a low anchor, feet a bit wider than hip-width, ribs over hips, arms straight holding a band in front of the hips, band running back between the legs to the anchor.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Hips pushed back, knees soft, shins near vertical, flat back tipped forward, arms straight between the legs holding the band, which runs back taut to a low anchor behind.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
summary: Trains a hip hinge and balance on one leg at a time.
equipment: none (a wall or chair for balance helps)
startingPosition: Stand on one foot, standing knee softly bent, the other foot just off the floor beside it. Rest one hand lightly on a wall or chair, the other on your hip. Hips level and square, eyes forward.
steps: Stand on one leg with the knee soft, one hand resting lightly on a wall or chair for balance.
Push your hips back as your free leg reaches straight back, body and back leg moving as one plank.
Keep your hips square to the floor so the toes of your back leg point down.
Lower until your hips stop moving back or you feel a strong stretch behind your standing thigh.
Drive your standing hip forward and bring your back leg down to stand tall; do all reps, then switch sides.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Hinge on the standing hip over two to three seconds as your back leg rises and your torso tips forward as one piece.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Push through your standing foot and bring your hips forward over one to two seconds to stand tall.

breathing: Breathe in and brace as you hinge. Breathe out as you push through your standing foot to stand tall.
cues: Body and back leg move as one plank.
Back toes point at the floor.
Standing knee soft, and it stays soft.
Reach your heel back, not up.

formChecks.check: Your head, back, hips and back heel form one straight line throughout, like a plank tipping on a pivot.
Both hips stay at the same height, and the toes of your back foot point straight down, not out to the side.
Your standing shin stays close to vertical with a soft knee bend that doesn't change through the rep.

mistakes.title: Hips opening to the side
mistakes.looksLike: As your back leg rises, that hip rotates up and out, and the back foot's toes turn out to the side instead of pointing down.
mistakes.why: Your pelvis twists instead of hinging, so the standing hip moves less and its glute and hamstring do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Point your back toes at the floor and keep both hip bones level, as if they were two headlights shining at the floor.
mistakes.cue: Hips level; back toes aim down.

mistakes.title: Body and back leg out of line
mistakes.looksLike: Your chest drops while your back leg stays low, or the leg kicks high while your chest stays up, so you fold at the free-leg hip.
mistakes.why: The movement has to happen at your standing hip. When the body bends elsewhere, the standing glute and hamstring do less.
mistakes.fix: Keep your torso and back leg in one line, like a plank tipping on a seesaw, and reach your back heel toward the wall behind you.
mistakes.cue: Chest and heel move like a seesaw.

mistakes.title: Standing knee locked or sinking
mistakes.looksLike: Your standing knee either snaps straight or bends deeper as you lower, so your hips drop down instead of moving back.
mistakes.why: A locked knee makes balance harder; a sinking knee turns it into a one-leg squat and takes work off your hamstring.
mistakes.fix: Set a slight bend in your standing knee before you start and keep that same angle for the whole rep.
mistakes.cue: Knee slightly bent the whole rep.

safety: Use a wall or chair for balance as long as you need it. Losing balance is normal; reset and continue.
Shorten the range if you can't keep your hips square or your back long. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
Train on a clear, non-slip floor, barefoot or in flat shoes.
easier: Hip Hinge
harder: Let go of the support and balance on your own

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing on one leg with a soft knee, the other foot just off the floor beside it, one hand resting lightly on the back of a chair, the other hand on the hip, body upright.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Hinged on the standing hip, standing knee soft, torso and back leg in one straight line nearly parallel to the floor, back toes pointing down, one hand lightly on the chair back.

name: Wall Push-Up
summary: Learn the push-up line and elbow path standing at a wall.
startingPosition: Face a wall, feet hip-width apart. Hands on the wall at about shoulder height, slightly wider than your shoulders, fingers up. Feet set back so your body leans in one straight line from head to heels. Eyes on the wall.
steps: Place your hands on the wall at about shoulder height, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your body leans in one straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, elbows angled back about 30–45°.
Stop when your chest is about a fist from the wall.
Press the wall away until your arms are straight, keeping your body in one line.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Bend your elbows and bring your chest toward the wall over two to three seconds, letting your shoulder blades come together.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Press the wall away over one to two seconds until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.

breathing: Breathe in as you lower toward the wall. Breathe out as you press the wall away.
cues: Move as one piece, like a plank.
Elbows back in an arrow, not a T.
Chest to a fist from the wall.
Push the wall away at the top.
Feet farther back makes it harder.

formChecks.check: Your ear, shoulder, hip and ankle stay in one straight line at the top and the bottom of every rep.
At the bottom, your chest is about a fist from the wall and your head has not reached ahead of your chest.
Your elbows angle down and back about 30–45° from your sides, an arrow shape, not straight out at shoulder height.

mistakes.title: Hips sagging toward the wall
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips reach the wall before your chest does, so your body bends at the waist into a shallow banana shape.
mistakes.why: Your trunk stops moving as one piece, your lower back arches, and your chest and arms travel less.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze your glutes and keep your ribs and pelvis moving together. If the line still breaks, step your feet a little closer.
mistakes.cue: Glutes tight, ribs and hips as one.

mistakes.title: Elbows flaring into a T
mistakes.looksLike: From behind, your elbows point straight out to the sides at shoulder height, near 90° from your torso, like the letter T.
mistakes.why: Your shoulders take more of the strain and your shoulder blades can't move freely, so the press is harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Keep your hands just outside your shoulders and let your elbows travel back about 30–45° from your sides, an arrow shape.
mistakes.cue: Elbows angled back, not straight out.

mistakes.title: Head reaching for the wall
mistakes.looksLike: Your chin pokes forward and your nose nears the wall while your chest stays well back.
mistakes.why: The rep looks deeper than it is, so your chest and arms only work through part of the range.
mistakes.fix: Keep your head in line with your body and your eyes on the wall. Let your chest lead toward the wall.
mistakes.cue: Head in line; let your chest lead.

safety: Wear shoes or stand on a surface with good grip so your feet cannot slide away from the wall.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in your shoulders, elbows or wrists, and shorten the range to what stays comfortable.
easier: Stand closer to the wall so you are more upright
harder: Incline Push-Up

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Leaning toward a wall in one straight line from head to heels, feet hip-width and set back from the wall, arms straight, palms flat on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than the shoulders.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Same straight body line, elbows bent and angled back about 45° from the torso, chest about a fist from the wall, head in line with the body, palms flat on the wall, heels down or slightly lifted.

name: Incline Push-Up
summary: A push-up with hands raised, so you can practice good form with less load.
startingPosition: Hands on the edge of a sturdy bench, table or counter, slightly wider than your shoulders and level with your chest. Feet back and hip-width apart, body in one straight line. Eyes on the surface just past your hands.
steps: Place your hands slightly wider than your shoulders on the edge of a stable raised surface.
Step your feet back so your body forms one straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the edge with your elbows angled back about 30–45°.
Stop when your chest is about a fist from the edge.
Press the surface away to return to the start, keeping your body in one line.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the edge over two to three seconds, letting your shoulder blades come together.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Press the surface away over one to two seconds until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.

breathing: Breathe in as you lower toward the edge. Breathe out as you press the surface away.
cues: Higher hands, easier rep. Lower hands, harder rep.
Elbows back in an arrow, not a T.
Chest leads; head stays in line.
Push the surface away at the top.

formChecks.check: Your ear, shoulder, hip and ankle stay in one straight line at the top and the bottom of every rep.
At the bottom, your chest is about a fist from the edge and your hands sit roughly level with your lower chest.
At the bottom, your elbows angle back toward your hips about 30–45° from your sides, not straight out at shoulder height.

mistakes.title: Hips sagging
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips drop below the line from shoulders to heels and your lower back arches as you lower.
mistakes.why: Your trunk stops moving as one piece, so your hips reach the edge first and your chest and arms do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze your glutes and keep your ribs down so ribs and pelvis move together. Use a higher surface if the line still breaks.
mistakes.cue: Glutes tight, ribs down.

mistakes.title: Elbows flaring straight out
mistakes.looksLike: At the bottom your elbows point straight out to the sides at shoulder height, near 90° from your torso, like the letter T.
mistakes.why: Your shoulders take more of the strain and your shoulder blades can't move freely, so the press is harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Set your hands just outside your shoulders, fingers forward, and let your elbows travel back about 30–45° from your sides.
mistakes.cue: Elbows back: an arrow, not a T.

mistakes.title: Using an unstable surface
mistakes.looksLike: The bench, chair or table shifts or rocks as you press, or your hands slide on a slick edge.
mistakes.why: You lose balance and control, and your effort goes into staying steady instead of pressing.
mistakes.fix: Use a kitchen counter, a heavy table or a bench pushed against a wall. Test it with your full weight before the first rep.
mistakes.cue: Pick a sturdy surface; test it first.

safety: Use a surface that cannot slide or tip, such as a kitchen counter or a bench pushed against a wall. Avoid chairs with wheels.
If your wrists are uncomfortable, grip the rounded edge of the surface or use a higher one. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Wall Push-Up
harder: Push-Up

frames.label: Top
