frames.pose: Body in one straight line from head to heels at an incline, arms straight, hands on the edge of a sturdy bench slightly wider than the shoulders, feet hip-width on the floor, head in line with the body.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Same straight body line, elbows bent and angled back about 45° from the torso, chest about a fist from the bench edge, hands level with the lower chest, head in line, feet planted.

name: Kneeling Push-Up
summary: A push-up from the knees that trains the full floor range with less load.
equipment: none (a mat or folded towel under the knees)
startingPosition: Kneel on a mat, hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders, under or just outside them, fingers forward. Hands far enough forward that knees, hips, shoulders and head make one line. Eyes just ahead of your hands.
steps: Kneel on a mat and place your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders.
Walk your hands forward until your knees, hips, shoulders and head form one straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor with your elbows angled back about 30–45°.
Stop when your chest is about a fist from the floor.
Press the floor away until your arms are straight, keeping the line from knees to head.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor over two to three seconds, letting your shoulder blades come together.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Press the floor away over one to two seconds until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.

breathing: Breathe in as you lower. Breathe out as you press the floor away, keeping your stomach braced.
cues: One straight line from knees to head.
Hips stay in line: not up, not down.
Elbows back in an arrow, not a T.
Chest to a fist from the floor.
Push the floor away at the top.

formChecks.check: Your knees, hips, shoulders and ear stay in one straight line. Your hips neither rise into a bend nor sag below it.
At the bottom, your chest is about a fist from the floor and your forearms are close to vertical, wrists under your elbows.
At the bottom, your elbows sit about 30–45° from your sides, an arrow shape, not a T.

mistakes.title: Hips piking up
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips stay high with a bend at the waist, so only your head and shoulders dip toward the floor.
mistakes.why: Your chest travels only a short way, and the rep turns into a shoulder dip instead of a full push-up.
mistakes.fix: Walk your hands farther forward and squeeze your glutes until your hips line up with your knees and shoulders. Lower as one piece.
mistakes.cue: Walk your hands out, hips in line.

mistakes.title: Hips sagging
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips drop below the line from knees to shoulders and your lower back arches as you lower.
mistakes.why: Your trunk stops moving as one piece, so your belly nears the floor before your chest does.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze your glutes and pull your ribs down toward your hips. Use a shorter range until the line holds.
mistakes.cue: Squeeze glutes, ribs toward hips.

mistakes.title: Elbows flaring into a T
mistakes.looksLike: At the bottom your elbows point straight out to the sides, near 90° from your torso, like the letter T.
mistakes.why: Your shoulders take more of the strain and your shoulder blades can't move freely, so the press is harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Set your hands just outside your shoulders, fingers forward, and let your elbows travel back about 30–45° from your sides.
mistakes.cue: Fingers forward, elbows angled back.

safety: Pad your knees with a mat or folded towel. If kneeling is still uncomfortable, use the incline push-up instead.
If your wrists ache, use push-up handles or hex dumbbells to keep them straight. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Incline Push-Up
harder: Push-Up

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Kneeling on a mat, arms straight, hands on the floor slightly wider than and under the shoulders, body in one straight line from knees to head, hips neither raised nor dropped, shins resting on the mat.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Same knee-to-head line, elbows bent and angled back about 45° from the torso, forearms near vertical, chest about a fist above the floor, head in line with the body, knees on the mat.

name: Push-Up
summary: Build upper-body pushing strength one controlled rep at a time.
startingPosition: High plank: hands slightly wider than your shoulders, under or just outside them, fingers forward. Legs straight, feet hip-width or closer. One straight line from head to heels, glutes tight, eyes just ahead of your hands.
steps: Begin in a high plank with hands near shoulder-width.
Lower under control while keeping body aligned.
Press the floor away to return to plank.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower your whole body as one piece over two to three seconds, until your chest is about a fist from the floor.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Press the floor away over one to two seconds until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.

breathing: Breathe in as you lower. Breathe out as you press the floor away, keeping your stomach braced.
cues: Elbows back in an arrow, not a T.
Chest to a fist from the floor.
Push the floor away at the top.
Stop the set when your form starts to change.

formChecks.check: Your ear, shoulder, hip and ankle stay in one straight line at the top and the bottom of every rep.
At the bottom, your chest is about a fist from the floor and your forearms are close to vertical, wrists under your elbows.
At the bottom, your elbows sit about 30–45° from your sides, an arrow shape, not a T.
Your shoulder blades slide together as you lower and spread apart as you press to the top.

mistakes.title: Sagging hips
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips drop below the line from shoulders to heels and your lower back arches, often in the last few reps of a set.
mistakes.why: Your trunk stops moving as one piece, so your hips reach the floor first and the push gets harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze your glutes and pull your ribs toward your hips so they move together. If the line still breaks, end the set.
mistakes.cue: Glutes squeezed, ribs pulled to hips.

mistakes.title: Flared elbows
mistakes.looksLike: At the bottom your elbows point straight out to the sides, near 90° from your torso, making a T with your body.
mistakes.why: Your shoulders take more of the strain and your shoulder blades can't move freely, so the press is harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Set your hands just outside your shoulders, fingers forward, and aim your elbows back about 30–45° from your sides, an arrow shape.
mistakes.cue: Hands outside shoulders, elbows back.

mistakes.title: Reduced control
mistakes.looksLike: Late in the set the reps speed up, you drop through the last few inches, or the depth shrinks to small bounces near the top.
mistakes.why: Momentum does the work instead of your chest and triceps, and short reps skip the bottom, where the push is hardest.
mistakes.fix: Lower for two to three seconds to the same depth every rep. End the set when you can't, even if you are short of your target.
mistakes.cue: Lower slowly to the same depth.

safety: If your wrists ache, use push-up handles or hex dumbbells to keep them straight, or put your hands on a raised surface.
Stop if you feel sharp pain. Shorten the range or switch to the incline push-up until it stays comfortable.
easier: Incline Push-Up
harder: Lower for three seconds and pause at the bottom

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: High plank, arms straight, hands on the floor slightly wider than and under the shoulders, body in one straight line from head to heels, feet hip-width, head in line with the spine.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Same straight line from head to heels, elbows bent and angled back about 45° from the torso, forearms near vertical, chest about a fist above the floor, hips level with the shoulders.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
summary: A dumbbell chest press from the floor, with a built-in stopping point.
startingPosition: Lie on your back on the floor, knees bent, feet flat. Dumbbells pressed up over your chest, arms straight, palms facing your feet or slightly in, wrists straight. Shoulder blades set back against the floor, eyes on the ceiling.
steps: Sit on the floor with the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back holding them against your chest.
Bend your knees, set your feet flat and press the dumbbells up over your chest.
Lower the dumbbells with your forearms vertical and your elbows about 45° from your torso.
Let your upper arms touch the floor lightly and pause for one second.
Press the dumbbells back up until your arms are straight over your chest.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower the dumbbells over two to three seconds, forearms vertical, until your upper arms touch the floor lightly.

phases.label: Pause
phases.text: Hold for about one second with your upper arms resting on the floor and your stomach braced.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Press up over one to two seconds until your arms are straight and the dumbbells are over your chest.

breathing: Breathe in as you lower and hold it through the pause. Breathe out as you press the dumbbells up.
cues: Elbows at 45°, not out in a T.
Touch the floor lightly. No bounce.

formChecks.check: At the bottom, your forearms are vertical, with each dumbbell straight above its elbow.
Your upper arms reach the floor and stay there for about a second before each press, with no bounce.
At the bottom, your elbows sit about 45° from your torso, an arrow shape, not a T.

mistakes.title: Elbows flaring into a T
mistakes.looksLike: Your elbows land on the floor straight out from your shoulders, near 90° from your torso, like the letter T.
mistakes.why: Your shoulders take more of the load and the dumbbells drift off line, which makes the press harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Before you lower, angle your elbows about 45° from your sides, with palms facing your feet or turned slightly in.
mistakes.cue: Angle elbows 45 degrees, then lower.

mistakes.title: Hips lifting off the floor
mistakes.looksLike: As you press, your hips lift off the floor and your back arches, so your body forms a bridge.
mistakes.why: Bridging shortens the press and shifts work away from your chest and triceps.
mistakes.fix: Keep your hips and lower back on the floor and your feet flat. If you have to bridge to finish a rep, use lighter dumbbells.
mistakes.cue: Hips down, press with your arms.

mistakes.title: Wrists bent back
mistakes.looksLike: Your wrists fold back so the dumbbells sit behind your forearms, knuckles pointing toward your head instead of the ceiling.
mistakes.why: The weight is off line with your forearms, so your wrists strain and less force goes into the press.
mistakes.fix: Grip the handle firmly and stack dumbbell over wrist and wrist over elbow, knuckles toward the ceiling.
mistakes.cue: Firm grip, knuckles to the ceiling.

safety: Pick a weight you can lower slowly and pause with on every rep. End the set when the dumbbells start to wobble or drift.
To finish, lower the dumbbells to your chest before setting them down. Don't drop them out to your sides.
If your shoulders are uncomfortable, turn your palms to face each other and keep your elbows closer to your sides.
easier: Use lighter dumbbells
harder: Lower over three seconds, then pause for two

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Lying on the back on a mat, knees bent and feet flat, arms straight holding two dumbbells above the chest, palms facing the feet, wrists straight.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Same lying position, elbows bent about 45° from the torso, upper arms resting lightly on the mat, forearms vertical, each dumbbell straight above its elbow, wrists straight.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
summary: A seated overhead press that builds shoulder and triceps strength.
equipment: two dumbbells and a chair with a back
startingPosition: Sit tall on a sturdy chair, back against the backrest, feet flat and hip-width apart. Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward or slightly in, forearms vertical. Ribs down, eyes forward.
steps: Sit tall with your back against the chair and your feet flat on the floor.
Bring the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms forward or slightly in, forearms vertical.
Brace your stomach and keep your ribs down so your back stays against the chair.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly back until your arms finish beside your ears.
Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height under control.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Press up and slightly back over one to two seconds until your arms are straight and beside your ears.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower the dumbbells to shoulder height over two to three seconds, keeping your forearms vertical.

breathing: Breathe in and brace with the dumbbells at your shoulders. Breathe out as you press up.
cues: Ribs down; back stays on the chair.
Finish with your arms beside your ears.

formChecks.check: At the top, the dumbbells are over your shoulders and your arms are beside your ears, not out in front of your face.
The gap between your lower back and the backrest stays the same as you press; it does not grow as you reach the top.
Each dumbbell stays directly above its elbow from shoulder height to the top, and both sides rise evenly.

mistakes.title: Arching the lower back
mistakes.looksLike: As the dumbbells go up, your ribs flare, your lower back peels off the chair, and your chest tilts toward the ceiling.
mistakes.why: Leaning back turns the lift into a partial chest press, so your shoulders skip the top of the overhead range.
mistakes.fix: Keep your ribs down and your back on the chair. Use lighter dumbbells so you can finish each rep without arching.
mistakes.cue: Lighter weight, back on the chair.

mistakes.title: Pressing out in front
mistakes.looksLike: At the top, the dumbbells finish in front of your face, with your arms angled forward instead of beside your ears.
mistakes.why: The weight sits ahead of your shoulders, so it is harder to balance and your shoulders work through a shorter range.
mistakes.fix: Press up and slightly back so your arms finish beside your ears, with the dumbbells over your shoulders.
mistakes.cue: Dumbbells finish over your shoulders.

mistakes.title: Forearms tilting out of line
mistakes.looksLike: From the front, your elbows flare out wide or pinch in, so the dumbbells sit outside or inside your elbows instead of above them.
mistakes.why: The weight pulls your forearms off line, so less of your effort goes straight up into the press.
mistakes.fix: Keep each dumbbell stacked over its wrist and elbow from shoulder height to the top, and lower only to shoulder height.
mistakes.cue: Stack dumbbell over wrist over elbow.

safety: Press only as high as you can while your ribs stay down and your back stays on the chair. If the top pinches your shoulder, stop short of it.
Use a chair that cannot roll or tip, and lift the dumbbells to your shoulders one at a time from your thighs.
Stop if you feel sharp pain. Palms facing slightly in is often more comfortable than palms straight forward.
easier: Use lighter dumbbells
harder: Press standing, with ribs down and glutes tight

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Seated tall on a chair, back against the backrest, feet flat hip-width, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward, forearms vertical, elbows slightly in front of the torso.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Same seated position, arms straight overhead, dumbbells over the shoulders, arms beside the ears, ribs down, lower back still against the backrest, feet flat.

name: Band Chest Press
summary: A standing chest press against a band anchored behind you.
equipment: resistance band anchored behind at chest height
startingPosition: Band anchored behind you at chest height, or wrapped around your upper back. Stand facing away in a staggered stance, knees soft. Handles beside your chest, elbows about 45° from your sides, wrists straight. Eyes forward.
steps: Anchor the band behind you at chest height, or wrap it around your upper back.
Face away from the anchor in a staggered stance, with tension in the band and the handles beside your chest.
Brace your stomach so your body stays still as the band pulls back.
Press the handles straight forward at chest height until your arms are straight.
Let the handles come back to your chest under control, elbows about 45° from your sides.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Press straight forward over one to two seconds until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades reach forward.

phases.label: Returning
phases.text: Let the handles come back to your chest over two to three seconds, keeping tension in the band.

breathing: Breathe out as you press forward. Breathe in as the handles come back to your chest.
cues: Elbows at 45°, not out in a T.
Body stays still; only your arms move.

formChecks.check: Your hands travel straight forward at chest height, in line with the band, and don't drift up toward your face.
Your torso stays upright with your head over your hips; it doesn't tip forward or rock back as you press.
As the handles return, your elbows stay angled down about 45° from your sides, not lifted to shoulder height.

mistakes.title: Leaning into the press
mistakes.looksLike: Your whole body tips forward from the ankles or hips as you press, so your bodyweight moves the band, not your arms.
mistakes.why: Leaning takes tension out of the band and shifts the work away from your chest and triceps.
mistakes.fix: Use a staggered stance, brace and keep your torso still. If you can't, use a lighter band or step closer to the anchor.
mistakes.cue: Staggered stance, brace, torso still.

mistakes.title: Elbows flaring into a T
mistakes.looksLike: As the handles come back, your elbows lift to shoulder height and point straight out to the sides, like the letter T.
mistakes.why: Your shoulders take more of the strain and your shoulder blades can't move freely, so the press is harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Keep your elbows angled down and back about 45° from your sides, an arrow shape, with your hands at chest height.
mistakes.cue: Elbows low and back, hands at chest.

mistakes.title: Letting the band snap back
mistakes.looksLike: Your hands fly back past your chest and your elbows shoot well behind your body as the band pulls.
mistakes.why: The return half stops doing useful work, and the band pulls your shoulders back past a range you can control.
mistakes.fix: Take two to three seconds to come back, and stop when your hands reach your chest, elbows just behind your torso.
mistakes.cue: Hands return slowly, stop at chest.

safety: Check the band for nicks or tears and make sure the anchor is firmly fixed and cannot slip before you lean into it.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in your shoulders or elbows. Use a lighter band or a shorter range until it is comfortable.
easier: Use a lighter band or step closer to the anchor
harder: Use a heavier band or step farther from the anchor

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing in a staggered stance facing away from a band anchored behind at chest height, torso upright, handles held beside the chest, elbows bent and angled about 45° from the torso.

frames.label: Press
frames.pose: Same staggered stance and upright torso, arms straight forward at chest height holding the band handles, band running back to the anchor at chest height.

name: Pike Push-Up
summary: A push-up with hips high that shifts the work toward your shoulders.
startingPosition: Inverted V: hands slightly wider than your shoulders, fingers forward, arms straight. Feet walked in so your hips are high, knees slightly bent if your hamstrings are tight. Head between your arms, eyes on the floor between your hands.
steps: Start in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Walk your feet toward your hands and lift your hips high into an inverted V.
Bend your elbows back at about 45° and lower the top of your head toward a point in front of your hands.
Stop with your head just above the floor, so your head and hands form a triangle.
Press the floor away to straighten your arms, keeping your hips high.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Bend your elbows and lower your head toward the floor in front of your hands over two to three seconds.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Press back up over one to two seconds until your arms are straight, keeping your hips high.

breathing: Breathe in as you lower your head toward the floor. Breathe out as you press back up.
cues: Head goes forward of your hands.
Head and hands make a triangle.
Elbows back at 45°, not out wide.
Push the floor away; hips stay up.

formChecks.check: Your hips stay high in an inverted V through the whole rep, with arms and torso close to one straight line at the top.
At the bottom, the top of your head is a few inches in front of your hands, so head and hands make a triangle on the floor.
Your elbows angle back about 45° from your torso as you lower, not straight out to the sides in a T.

mistakes.title: Hips dropping toward a plank
mistakes.looksLike: As you lower, your hips sink and your body flattens toward a plank, so your chest, not your head, heads for the floor.
mistakes.why: The press turns into a regular push-up, and your shoulders lose the overhead angle the exercise is meant to train.
mistakes.fix: Walk your feet closer to your hands and keep your hips high. Think about lowering your head, not your chest.
mistakes.cue: Walk your feet in, hips stay high.

mistakes.title: Head dropping behind the hands
mistakes.looksLike: Your head lowers straight down between or behind your hands, and your forearms lean back toward your feet.
mistakes.why: Your forearms tilt off vertical, so your shoulders can't press in a straight line and the rep is harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Aim the top of your head at a spot a few inches in front of your hands, so your head and hands make a triangle.
mistakes.cue: Top of head aims ahead of your hands.

mistakes.title: Elbows flaring out wide
mistakes.looksLike: From the front, your elbows point straight out to the sides, near 90° from your torso, as your head lowers.
mistakes.why: Your shoulders end up in a weaker pressing position and your shoulder blades can't move freely.
mistakes.fix: Set your hands slightly wider than your shoulders, fingers forward, and let your elbows track back about 45°.
mistakes.cue: Elbows aim back as your head lowers.

safety: If you can't lower with control, put your hands on a sturdy step or bench to reduce the load.
Lower slowly and stop with your head just above the floor. A folded towel under your head is fine while you learn.
If your wrists ache, use push-up handles or hex dumbbells to keep them straight. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Push-Up
harder: Put your feet on a low step to raise your hips

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Inverted V: hips high, arms straight, hands on the floor slightly wider than the shoulders, legs straight or knees slightly bent, heels lifted, head between the upper arms.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Hips still high, elbows bent and angled back about 45°, top of the head just above the floor a few inches in front of the hands, head and hands forming a triangle, heels lifted.

name: Prone Y Raise
summary: Teaches your shoulder blades to move back and down, with no equipment.
startingPosition: Lie face down on a mat, legs straight and relaxed, forehead on a folded towel, eyes on the floor. Arms overhead in a Y, each about 30–45° out from the line of your body, thumbs up, elbows straight but not locked.
steps: Lie face down on a mat with your arms overhead in a Y, thumbs pointing up.
Rest your forehead on a folded towel so your neck stays long.
Draw your shoulder blades back and down toward your back pockets.
Lift both arms a few centimeters off the mat, leading with your thumbs.
Pause for one to two seconds, then lower your arms slowly to the mat.

phases.label: Lifting
phases.text: Set your shoulder blades back and down, then raise both arms a few centimeters over about one second.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Hold the top for one to two seconds, shoulders away from your ears.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower your arms to the mat over two seconds and let them rest for a moment.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift and hold, and breathe in as you lower. Don't hold your breath.
cues: Shoulder blades down toward your back pockets.

formChecks.check: Your forehead stays on the towel and your chest and hips stay on the mat; only your arms rise, a few centimeters at most.
Your arms hold a Y, each about 30–45° out from the line of your body, thumbs up, elbows straight but not locked.
At the top, your shoulder blades slide down and toward each other, and the space between your ears and shoulders stays open.

mistakes.title: Arching the lower back
mistakes.looksLike: Your chest and head peel off the mat and your lower back arches so your arms can rise higher.
mistakes.why: The lift comes from your lower back instead of your shoulder blades, so your upper back does less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Keep your forehead on the towel and your chest on the mat, and lightly squeeze your glutes. Lift only as high as your shoulder blades take your arms.
mistakes.cue: Chest on the mat, small arm lift.

mistakes.title: Shrugging toward the ears
mistakes.looksLike: Seen from above, your shoulders ride up toward your ears as your arms lift, and the gap between ears and shoulders closes.
mistakes.why: Your upper traps take over, and the lower muscles between your shoulder blades, the ones this targets, do less.
mistakes.fix: Before each lift, slide your shoulder blades down toward your back pockets. Hold that position and lift a little lower if you need to.
mistakes.cue: Shoulders down first, then lift.

mistakes.title: Lifting the head to look ahead
mistakes.looksLike: Your forehead leaves the towel and your chin pokes forward so you look ahead, bending your neck back as your arms lift.
mistakes.why: Your neck works to hold your head up, and it gets harder to feel and control your shoulder blades.
mistakes.fix: Leave your forehead on the towel and your eyes on the floor. Think of a long neck, from the back of your head to your upper back.
mistakes.cue: Eyes on the floor, neck long.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain or a pinch in the shoulder. Lift a smaller range, widen the Y slightly, or lift one arm at a time.
If lying flat strains your lower back or neck, put a thin pillow under your stomach and keep your forehead on the towel.
easier: Lift one arm at a time, a smaller range
harder: Seated Band Row

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Lying face down on a mat, legs straight. Head down: face to the floor, forehead resting on a small folded towel, eyes on the floor. Arms straight overhead in a wide Y, resting on the mat, thumbs up.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Same position, forehead still on the towel and face to the floor, chest and hips on the mat. Both straight arms lifted only a few centimeters off the mat, a small lift, with the shoulder blades drawn down and back.

name: Seated Band Row
summary: Trains your back to pull your elbows back while you sit tall.
startingPosition: Sit tall on the floor, legs straight or slightly bent, band looped around the soles of your feet. One end in each hand, palms facing in, arms straight at lower-chest height, band slightly taut. Look straight ahead.
steps: Sit tall on the floor with your legs straight or slightly bent and loop the middle of the band around your feet.
Hold one end in each hand, palms facing each other, arms straight with a little tension in the band.
Pull your elbows back along your sides toward your hips until your hands reach your lower ribs.
Pause for a second with your shoulder blades drawn together and your chest tall.
Let your arms straighten slowly, allowing your shoulder blades to slide forward without rounding your back.

phases.label: Pulling
phases.text: Pull your elbows back along your sides to your lower ribs in about one second, then pause for one second.

phases.label: Returning
phases.text: Let your arms straighten over two seconds until your shoulder blades spread forward, chest still tall.

breathing: Breathe out as you pull and breathe in as your arms return.
cues: Shoulders down, away from your ears.

formChecks.check: Your torso stays upright, shoulders stacked over hips, from the start of each rep to the finish, with no rocking back.
At the finish, your elbows are just behind your torso and your hands are at your lower ribs, not your chest.
At full reach, your arms are straight and your shoulders drift slightly forward while your chest stays tall.

mistakes.title: Rocking back to pull
mistakes.looksLike: Your torso swings from upright to leaning back 20° or more on each pull, then tips forward as the band returns.
mistakes.why: Your body weight stretches the band instead of your back muscles, so they do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Keep your shoulders stacked over your hips so only your arms move. If you can't, use a lighter band or hold it with more slack.
mistakes.cue: Torso still; only your arms move.

mistakes.title: Slumping instead of sitting tall
mistakes.looksLike: Your lower back rounds into a C, your pelvis rolls back and your chest drops toward your legs.
mistakes.why: From a slumped seat your shoulder blades can't draw back fully, so the pull becomes mostly an arm movement.
mistakes.fix: Bend your knees a little or sit on a folded towel or cushion so you can sit tall with your shoulders over your hips.
mistakes.cue: Bend your knees or sit on a cushion.

mistakes.title: Shrugging the shoulders
mistakes.looksLike: As you pull, your shoulders rise toward your ears and your hands finish near your chest instead of your lower ribs.
mistakes.why: Your upper traps and arms take over, and your lats and mid-back do less.
mistakes.fix: Set your shoulders down before each rep. Pull your elbows back toward your hips and finish with your hands at your lower ribs.
mistakes.cue: Shoulders down, hands to lower ribs.

safety: Check the band for nicks or tears before each session, and keep it centered on the soles of your feet so it can't slip off.
If sitting on the floor bothers your back or hips, sit on a cushion with your knees bent. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Use a lighter band or hold it with more slack
harder: Supported Dumbbell Row

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Sitting tall on a mat, legs straight with knees slightly bent, band looped around the soles of the feet. Arms straight forward at lower-chest height holding the band ends, slight tension.

frames.label: Finish
frames.pose: Same seated position, torso upright over the hips. Elbows pulled back close to the sides, just behind the torso, hands at the lower ribs, shoulder blades drawn together.

name: Band Pull-Apart
summary: Trains your rear shoulders and upper back to pull your arms apart.
startingPosition: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, knees soft. Hold the band with both hands, palms down, about shoulder-width apart. Arms straight but not locked at chest height, band slightly taut. Shoulders down, eyes forward.
steps: Stand tall and hold a light band with both hands, palms down, about shoulder-width apart.
Raise your arms in front of you to chest height, straight but not locked.
Spread your hands apart and pull the band toward your chest until your arms are out to your sides.
Pause for a second with your shoulder blades drawn together and your shoulders down.
Bring your hands back together slowly, keeping some tension in the band.

phases.label: Pulling apart
phases.text: Spread your hands out to the sides in about one second until the band reaches your chest, then pause for one second.

phases.label: Returning
phases.text: Bring your hands back to shoulder-width over two seconds, keeping a little tension in the band.

breathing: Breathe out as you pull the band apart and breathe in as your hands come back together.
cues: Spread the band to your chest.

formChecks.check: At the finish, your arms form a T at chest height with elbows nearly straight, and the band reaches or nearly reaches your chest.
Your ribs stay stacked over your hips; the band moves toward you, not your chest toward the band.
Your shoulders stay level and low, with clear space between your shoulders and ears at the finish.

mistakes.title: Shrugging toward the ears
mistakes.looksLike: As the band stretches, your shoulders rise and the space between your shoulders and ears shrinks, most of all at the end of the pull.
mistakes.why: Your upper traps take over, and your rear shoulders and the muscles between your shoulder blades do less.
mistakes.fix: Set your shoulders down before each rep. Use a lighter band or start with your hands wider so you can finish without shrugging.
mistakes.cue: Shoulders down before each pull.

mistakes.title: Arching the lower back
mistakes.looksLike: At the end of the pull, your ribs flare, your chest pushes forward and your lower back arches as you lean back.
mistakes.why: Leaning back moves your body toward the band instead of moving the band with your shoulders, so they do less.
mistakes.fix: Brace your stomach and keep your ribs stacked over your hips. Stop the pull when the band reaches your chest.
mistakes.cue: Ribs over hips; stop at your chest.

mistakes.title: Bending the elbows
mistakes.looksLike: Your elbows bend to 90° or more as you pull, and your hands end near your shoulders, more like a row than a pull-apart.
mistakes.why: Bent arms shorten the lever and shift work toward your arms and lats, so your rear shoulders do less.
mistakes.fix: Keep a soft, fixed bend in your elbows from start to finish. If you can't, use a lighter band or start with your hands wider.
mistakes.cue: Elbows keep one soft, fixed bend.

safety: Check the band for nicks or tears before each session and replace a worn band, since it works close to your face.
If you feel a pinch at the front of the shoulder, use a lighter band, shorten the range or pull toward your lower chest. Stop if pain is sharp.
easier: Use a lighter band or start with hands wider
harder: Band Face Pull

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing tall, feet hip-width apart, knees soft. Arms straight forward at chest height, hands shoulder-width apart, palms down, holding a light band with slight tension.

frames.label: Finish
frames.pose: Same stance. Arms spread out to the sides at chest height in a T, elbows soft, band stretched across the front of the chest, shoulders low.

name: Band Face Pull
summary: Trains your rear shoulders and upper back with a high pull to your face.
equipment: resistance band anchored at face height
startingPosition: Band anchored at face height. Stand facing it in a staggered stance, knees soft, ribs over hips. One end in each hand, thumbs pointing back toward you, arms straight at face height, band taut. Eyes forward.
steps: Anchor the band at face height and hold one end in each hand, thumbs pointing back toward you.
Step back into a staggered stance until the band is taut with your arms straight in front of your face.
Pull the band toward your eyes, leading with your elbows high and out to the sides.
Finish with your hands beside your ears in a double-biceps position and pause briefly.
Let your arms straighten slowly back toward the anchor.

phases.label: Pulling
phases.text: Pull the band toward your eyes over about one second, elbows high and wide, until your hands are beside your ears.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Pause for one second in the double-biceps position, shoulders down.

phases.label: Returning
phases.text: Let your arms straighten toward the anchor over two seconds, keeping tension in the band.

breathing: Breathe out as you pull the band to your face and breathe in as your arms return.
cues: Pull to your eyes, elbows high and wide.

formChecks.check: At the finish, your elbows are about level with your shoulders and your hands are at eye level beside your head, not at your chest.
At the finish, your upper arms point out to the sides and your forearms point up, elbows bent about 90°, like a double-biceps pose.
Your torso stays upright, ribs over hips, and does not lean back as the band comes toward you.

mistakes.title: Elbows dropping into a row
mistakes.looksLike: Your elbows sink below shoulder height and stay near your sides, so the band ends at your chest or chin, not your eyes.
mistakes.why: With low elbows your lats and arms do most of the pulling, and your rear shoulders and upper back do less.
mistakes.fix: Keep your elbows high and wide, about level with your shoulders. Aim for your eyes or forehead, and use a lighter band if you can't reach.
mistakes.cue: Elbows level with your shoulders.

mistakes.title: Hands finishing below the elbows
mistakes.looksLike: At the end of the pull, your forearms point forward or down, hands lower than elbows, instead of up beside your head.
mistakes.why: Without turning your hands up and back, you miss the outward rotation that works the back of your shoulders.
mistakes.fix: Finish each rep in a double-biceps pose: upper arms out to the sides, elbows bent about 90°, hands beside your ears, thumbs back.
mistakes.cue: Hands finish beside your ears.

mistakes.title: Leaning back to pull
mistakes.looksLike: Your torso tips back 15° or more as you pull, and your hips push forward to help bring the band toward you.
mistakes.why: Your body weight does the pulling, so your shoulders and upper back get less work.
mistakes.fix: Use a staggered stance with your ribs stacked over your hips, and step closer to the anchor or use a lighter band to cut the tension.
mistakes.cue: Staggered stance, less band tension.

safety: Close the door fully, with the anchor on the hinge side and the door opening away from you, and check the band for nicks or tears.
If you feel a pinch at the top or front of the shoulder, lower the anchor slightly, use a lighter band or shorten the range. Stop if pain is sharp.
easier: Band Pull-Apart
harder: Pause for two seconds in the finish position

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing in a staggered stance facing a door anchor at face height. Arms straight forward at face height holding the band ends, thumbs pointing back, band taut, torso upright.

frames.label: Finish
frames.pose: Same stance, torso upright. Upper arms out to the sides at shoulder height, elbows bent about 90°, hands beside the ears, forearms vertical, band stretched to eye level.

name: Supported Dumbbell Row
summary: Trains your back to pull, with one hand supported for stability.
startingPosition: Hand and same-side knee on a bench, or the hand only with a staggered stance. Hand under shoulder, back flat and roughly parallel to the floor, eyes on the floor. Dumbbell in the free hand, hanging under your shoulder.
steps: Brace one hand on a stable support.
Keep back controlled, pull dumbbell toward hip.
Lower slowly with control.

phases.label: Pulling
phases.text: Pull your elbow back toward your hip in about one second until it passes your torso.

phases.label: Pause
phases.text: Hold for about one second with your shoulder down and both shoulders level.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower over two to three seconds to a full reach, letting your shoulder blade slide forward.

breathing: Breathe out as you pull and breathe in as you lower. Keep your stomach braced so your back stays still.
cues: Elbow to hip, not hand to shoulder.
Chest to the floor, shoulders level.
All reps on one side, then switch.

formChecks.check: Your back stays flat and roughly parallel to the floor, with your head in line, from the first rep to the last.
At the top, your elbow is just past your torso and the dumbbell is beside your lower ribs or hip, not your armpit.
Your shoulders stay level; the working shoulder doesn't rise or turn toward the ceiling as you pull.

mistakes.title: Twisting trunk
mistakes.looksLike: As you pull, your chest turns toward the ceiling on the working side and that shoulder finishes clearly higher than the supported one, so the shoulders are tilted, not level.
mistakes.why: Rotating your torso lifts the weight with your body, so your back muscles move it through less range.
mistakes.fix: Keep both shoulders level and your chest facing the floor. If you have to twist to finish the rep, use a lighter dumbbell.
mistakes.cue: Both shoulders level, chest down.

mistakes.title: Rounding the back
mistakes.looksLike: Your upper back hunches into a big round curve and your head hangs down toward the floor, so your back is clearly no longer flat as you pull.
mistakes.why: A rounded back gives your shoulder blade nothing steady to pull against, so your arm does more of the work and your lats do less.
mistakes.fix: Before each rep, push the bench away with your support hand and get long from head to tailbone. If your back rounds as you pull, use a lighter dumbbell.
mistakes.cue: Back flat, head in line.

mistakes.title: Pulling toward the shoulder
mistakes.looksLike: The dumbbell travels straight up toward your armpit or chest, your elbow flares away from your side and your shoulder rises toward your ear.
mistakes.why: That path shifts work to your upper traps and arm, and your lats do less of the pull.
mistakes.fix: Think elbow to hip: pull the dumbbell back in a slight arc toward your hip pocket, upper arm close to your side, shoulder down.
mistakes.cue: Elbow back toward your hip pocket.

safety: Use a stable bench, or a sturdy chair pushed against a wall, and keep your supporting hand under your shoulder.
If your lower back is uncomfortable, use a higher support so you are less bent over. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
Choose a dumbbell you can pause with at the top and lower slowly on every rep.
easier: Seated Band Row
harder: Pause for two seconds at the top of each rep

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Left hand and left knee on a flat bench, right foot on the floor. Back flat and parallel to the floor, right arm hanging straight below the shoulder holding a dumbbell.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Same support position, back flat, shoulders level. Right elbow pulled back past the torso toward the hip, upper arm close to the side, dumbbell beside the lower ribs.

name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
summary: Trains your back to row while you hold a hip hinge without support.
startingPosition: Feet hip-width apart, knees soft, hinged at the hips so your torso is about 30–45° above horizontal. Back flat, neck in line, eyes on the floor a few feet ahead. Dumbbells hang under your shoulders, palms facing in.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Soften your knees and hinge at the hips until your torso is about 30–45° above horizontal, back flat.
Let the dumbbells hang straight below your shoulders with your arms long.
Pull both elbows back toward your hips until they pass your torso, then pause briefly.
Lower the dumbbells slowly to a full reach while your torso stays still.

phases.label: Pulling
phases.text: Pull both elbows back toward your hips in about one second until they pass your torso, then pause for one second.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower over two to three seconds to a full reach, letting your shoulder blades slide forward while your torso stays still.

breathing: Brace before each pull and breathe out as you row. Breathe in as you lower.
cues: Shoulders down, pause at the top.

formChecks.check: Your torso holds the same angle, about 30–45° above horizontal, on every rep; your chest doesn't rise as you pull.
Your back stays flat from hips to head, knees soft, and the dumbbells start directly under your shoulders.
At the top, your elbows are just past your torso and the dumbbells are beside your lower ribs, not your chest.
Both dumbbells rise together, elbows close to your sides, and your shoulders stay level and away from your ears.

mistakes.title: Standing up to finish the rep
mistakes.looksLike: Your torso rises from about 45° toward upright as you pull, so the dumbbells finish near your stomach with your chest lifted.
mistakes.why: Standing up turns part of each rep into a hip movement and leaves your back muscles less to do.
mistakes.fix: Pick a torso angle and keep it for the whole set. Use lighter dumbbells, or the supported row if holding the hinge is the hard part.
mistakes.cue: Hold your torso angle the whole set.

mistakes.title: Rounding the back
mistakes.looksLike: Your back curves into a C from hips to head, your head drops and the dumbbells drift forward in front of your knees.
mistakes.why: From a rounded position your shoulder blades can't draw back fully, and the hinge gets harder to hold as you tire.
mistakes.fix: Brace your stomach, push your hips back and keep a long line from head to hips. Raise your torso a little or bend your knees more to stay flat.
mistakes.cue: Brace; long line from head to hips.

mistakes.title: Pulling toward the chest
mistakes.looksLike: Your elbows flare out wide, the dumbbells travel straight up toward your chest and your shoulders rise toward your ears.
mistakes.why: That path shifts work to your upper traps and arms, and your lats do less of the pull.
mistakes.fix: Pull your elbows back toward your hips, close to your sides, and keep your shoulders down. Finish with the dumbbells beside your lower ribs.
mistakes.cue: Elbows close, weights to lower ribs.

safety: If your lower back tires before your upper back, rest sooner, raise your torso slightly, or switch to the supported row.
Use dumbbells light enough to pause at the top of every rep. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
easier: Supported Dumbbell Row
harder: Pause for two seconds at the top

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Feet hip-width apart, knees soft, hips back, torso hinged to about 40° above horizontal, back flat, head in line. Arms straight, a dumbbell in each hand hanging below the shoulders.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Same hinge and torso angle. Both elbows pulled back past the torso, upper arms close to the sides, dumbbells beside the lower ribs, shoulder blades drawn together.

name: Band Lat Pulldown
summary: Trains your lats to pull your elbows down, using a band anchored high.
startingPosition: Band anchored high on a closed door. Kneel tall or sit facing it, far enough back that the band is taut with your arms straight up and slightly forward. Hands shoulder-width or a bit wider, chest up, eyes forward.
steps: Anchor the band high on a closed door and hold one end in each hand.
Kneel or sit facing the door, far enough back that the band is taut with your arms straight up and slightly forward.
Sit tall with your chest up, leaning back only slightly.
Draw your shoulders down, then pull your elbows down to the sides of your ribs and pause briefly.
Let your arms rise slowly until they are straight again.

phases.label: Pulling
phases.text: Draw your shoulders down, then pull your elbows to the sides of your ribs in about one second and pause for one second.

phases.label: Returning
phases.text: Let your arms rise over two seconds until they are straight and your shoulder blades lift slightly toward the anchor.

breathing: Breathe out as you pull down and breathe in as your arms rise.
cues: Elbows to the sides of your ribs.
Two seconds on the way up.

formChecks.check: Your torso stays nearly upright, leaning back no more than about 15°, from the start of each rep to the finish.
At the bottom, your elbows are beside your ribs and your shoulder blades have moved down, away from your ears.
At the top, your arms are straight and your shoulder blades rise slightly toward the anchor before the next pull.

mistakes.title: Leaning far back
mistakes.looksLike: Your torso tips back 30° or more as you pull, and the band comes toward your chest like a row instead of down to your ribs.
mistakes.why: Leaning back turns the pulldown into a row and lets your body weight help, so your lats do less of the pull down.
mistakes.fix: Keep your torso nearly upright with only a slight lean. Move closer to the door or use a lighter band if you need to lean to finish.
mistakes.cue: Torso almost upright the whole pull.

mistakes.title: Shoulders stuck up by the ears
mistakes.looksLike: Your shoulders stay hunched up through the pull, and your elbows stop around shoulder height instead of reaching your ribs.
mistakes.why: Without your shoulder blades moving down, your arms do most of the work and your lats get less.
mistakes.fix: Start each rep by drawing your shoulders down away from your ears, then pull your elbows down to the sides of your ribs.
mistakes.cue: Shoulders away from ears, then pull.

mistakes.title: Crunching the chest down
mistakes.looksLike: Your chest drops and your upper back rounds as you pull, like a crunch, and your elbows finish in front of your body.
mistakes.why: Curling forward lets your abs and body weight help, and your lats work through less range.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest up toward the anchor and finish with your elbows beside your ribs, slightly behind your torso.
mistakes.cue: Chest tall, elbows end by your ribs.

safety: Put the door anchor near the top on the hinge side, close the door fully so it opens away from you, and check the band for nicks or tears.
Kneel on a mat or cushion if your knees are uncomfortable. Stop if you feel sharp pain in your shoulder.
easier: Use a lighter band or move closer to the door
harder: Pause for two seconds at the bottom

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Kneeling tall on a mat facing a closed door with a high anchor. Arms straight up and slightly forward holding the band ends, band taut, torso upright, chest up.

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Same kneeling position, torso upright with a slight lean back. Elbows pulled down beside the ribs, hands near shoulder height, band stretched down from the anchor.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Fly
summary: Trains your rear shoulders and upper back to open your arms out wide.
startingPosition: Feet hip-width apart, knees soft, hinged at the hips with your torso about 45° above horizontal or lower, back flat. Light dumbbells hang under your chest, palms facing in, elbows slightly bent. Eyes on the floor ahead.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and knees soft, holding a light dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is about 45° above horizontal or lower, back flat, dumbbells under your chest.
Set a slight bend in your elbows and keep it fixed for the whole set.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides, leading with your elbows, to shoulder height or a little below.
Pause briefly, then lower the dumbbells slowly back under your chest.

phases.label: Raising
phases.text: Lift the dumbbells out to the sides in about one second, elbows leading, to shoulder height or a little below, then pause for one second.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower the dumbbells under your chest over two to three seconds, keeping the elbow bend fixed.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift the dumbbells and breathe in as you lower them.

formChecks.check: At the top, your arms make a wide T with the same slight elbow bend, and your hands are level with or just below your shoulders.
Your torso holds the same angle and your back stays flat on every rep; your chest doesn't rise as the dumbbells go up.
Your shoulders stay down, with clear space between your ears and shoulders at the top of each rep.

mistakes.title: Swinging the dumbbells
mistakes.looksLike: Your chest bobs up as the dumbbells fly up, and they drop back down in under a second.
mistakes.why: Momentum lifts the weight, so your rear shoulders work for only part of each rep.
mistakes.fix: Use lighter dumbbells. Lift in about one second, pause at shoulder height or just below, and lower over two to three seconds.
mistakes.cue: Lighter weights, pause at the top.

mistakes.title: Bending the elbows into a row
mistakes.looksLike: Your elbows bend from a slight bend to 90° or more as you lift, pulling the dumbbells up and back like a row.
mistakes.why: Bent arms shorten the lever and shift work to your mid-back and biceps, so your rear shoulders do less.
mistakes.fix: Set a slight elbow bend before the first rep and keep it. Think of opening your arms wide, and use lighter dumbbells if you can't.
mistakes.cue: Fixed slight bend; open arms wide.

mistakes.title: Shrugging toward the ears
mistakes.looksLike: As the dumbbells rise, your shoulders creep up toward your ears and the dumbbells go above shoulder height.
mistakes.why: Your upper traps take over, and your rear shoulders and the muscles between your shoulder blades do less.
mistakes.fix: Keep your neck long and shoulders down. Lead with your elbows out to the sides and stop at shoulder height or a little below.
mistakes.cue: Lead out with elbows, shoulders low.

safety: Start with light dumbbells; the rear shoulders are small muscles and handle far less weight than a row. Stop if you feel sharp pain.
If bending over bothers your lower back, rest your chest on an incline bench or swap to the prone Y raise.
easier: Prone Y Raise
harder: Pause for two seconds at the top

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Hinged at the hips, torso about 45° above horizontal, knees soft, back flat. Arms hanging under the chest with a slight elbow bend, a light dumbbell in each hand, palms facing in.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Same hinge. Arms raised out to the sides to just below shoulder height, elbows slightly bent and leading, palms facing the floor, shoulder blades drawn together.

name: Kneeling Plank
summary: Teaches you to hold a straight, braced trunk with your knees on the floor.
startingPosition: Kneel on a mat with your forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders, forearms parallel or hands lightly clasped. Walk your knees back until knees, hips and head line up. Look at the floor just ahead of your hands.
steps: Set your forearms on the floor with your elbows directly under your shoulders.
Walk your knees back until your knees, hips, shoulders and head form one straight line.
Squeeze your glutes and tuck your ribs down toward your hips to brace your trunk.
Hold the line and breathe steadily for the target time.
End the hold when your hips sag or pike, then sit back toward your heels to rest.

phases.label: Set up
phases.text: Take about 5 seconds to line up from knees to head, then squeeze your glutes and brace.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Hold for the target time with slow, steady breaths. End the hold as soon as your hips start to sag or pike.

phases.label: Release
phases.text: Sit back toward your heels over about 2 seconds, then rest.

breathing: Breathe slowly through your nose or pursed lips while your stomach stays braced. If you're holding your breath, shorten the hold.
cues: One straight line, knees to head.
Squeeze your glutes, tuck your ribs down.
Push the floor away with your forearms.
Eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands.

formChecks.check: Your knees, hips, shoulders and ears sit on one straight line, with no dip at the lower back and no peak at the hips.
Your elbows are directly under your shoulders, so your upper arms are vertical.
Your head stays in line with your back, eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands, not looking up.

mistakes.title: Hips sagging
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips drop below the line from knees to shoulders and your lower back arches, so your stomach hangs toward the floor.
mistakes.why: The arch shifts the work from your abs to your lower back, so the hold stops training trunk control.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze your glutes and tuck your ribs toward your hips until the line is straight. If the sag comes back, end the hold there.
mistakes.cue: Glutes tight, ribs toward hips.

mistakes.title: Hips piking up
mistakes.looksLike: Your seat rises above the line from knees to shoulders, so you bend at the hips and drift back toward an all-fours position.
mistakes.why: Bending at the hips shortens the lever and props you up on your knees, so your abs barely have to work.
mistakes.fix: Walk your knees back a little and lower your hips until knees, hips and shoulders line up. You should feel your stomach working.
mistakes.cue: Knees back a bit, hips down in line.

mistakes.title: Chest sinking between the shoulders
mistakes.looksLike: Your chest drops toward the floor and your shoulder blades pinch together, so your upper back dips between your shoulders.
mistakes.why: Your weight hangs on your shoulder joints instead of the muscles around your shoulder blades holding you up.
mistakes.fix: Push the floor away with your forearms until your upper back is flat, and keep your elbows under your shoulders.
mistakes.cue: Forearms press down, upper back flat.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. If your knees are uncomfortable, kneel on a folded mat or towel.
If your lower back aches during the hold, end the set early and shorten the next one.
easier: Shorter holds, such as 10 seconds, with rests between
harder: Front Plank

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: On all fours on a mat, forearms on the mat with elbows under the shoulders, knees under the hips, back flat, gaze at the floor.

frames.label: Hold
frames.pose: Forearms on the mat, elbows under the shoulders, knees on the mat and walked back so knees, hips, shoulders and head form one straight line, lower legs resting on the mat, gaze just ahead of the hands.

name: Front Plank
summary: Teaches you to hold your trunk straight and braced, from ears to ankles.
startingPosition: Forearms on the floor with elbows directly under your shoulders, forearms parallel or hands clasped. Legs straight behind you, feet about hip-width apart, up on your toes. Look at the floor just ahead of your hands.
steps: Place your forearms on the floor with your elbows directly under your shoulders.
Step your feet back one at a time until your body forms a straight line from ears to ankles.
Squeeze your glutes and tuck your ribs down toward your hips to brace your trunk.
Hold the line and breathe steadily for the target time.
End the hold when your hips sag or pike, and lower your knees to the floor to rest.

phases.label: Set up
phases.text: Take about 5 seconds to step your feet back, line up from ears to ankles and brace.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Hold for the target time with slow, steady breaths. End the hold as soon as your hips start to sag or pike.

phases.label: Release
phases.text: Lower your knees to the floor over about 2 seconds, then rest.

breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily without letting your stomach go loose. If you catch yourself holding your breath, shorten the hold.
cues: One straight line, ears to ankles.
Squeeze your glutes, tuck your ribs down.
Push the floor away with your forearms.
Eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands.
Shaking is normal; sagging is the signal to stop.

formChecks.check: Your ears, shoulders, hips, knees and ankles sit on one straight line, with no dip at the lower back and no peak at the hips.
Your elbows are directly under your shoulders, so your upper arms are vertical.
Your head stays in line with your back, eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands, not looking up.

mistakes.title: Hips sagging
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips drop below the line from shoulders to ankles and your lower back arches, so your stomach hangs toward the floor.
mistakes.why: The arch shifts the work from your abs to your lower back, so the hold stops training trunk control.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze your glutes and tuck your ribs toward your hips until you're straight again. If the sag comes back, end the hold there.
mistakes.cue: Ribs to hips, glutes squeezed.

mistakes.title: Hips piking up
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips rise above the line from shoulders to ankles, so your body forms an upside-down V and more weight shifts onto your arms.
mistakes.why: Bending at the hips shortens the lever, so your abs barely have to work to hold you up.
mistakes.fix: Lower your hips until they're level with your shoulders, then squeeze your glutes. Check the line on video or in a mirror at your side.
mistakes.cue: Hips down, level with your shoulders.

mistakes.title: Head hanging down
mistakes.looksLike: Your head drops below the line of your back, chin tucked toward your chest, and your eyes look back at your knees or feet.
mistakes.why: A hanging head pulls your upper back into a curve, so the straight line from ears to ankles breaks at the top.
mistakes.fix: Lift your head until your ears line up with your shoulders, and look at the floor just ahead of your hands.
mistakes.cue: Ears in line with your shoulders.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. If your lower back aches, end the hold early and switch to the kneeling plank.
If your elbows are sore on a hard floor, put a mat or folded towel under your forearms.
easier: Kneeling Plank
harder: Lift one foot for 2–3 seconds, alternating sides

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Kneeling with forearms on a mat, elbows under the shoulders, both knees on the mat behind the hips, ready to step back into the plank.

frames.label: Hold
frames.pose: Forearms on the mat, elbows under the shoulders, legs straight with feet hip-width apart on the toes; ears, shoulders, hips, knees and ankles in one straight line, gaze at the floor just ahead of the hands.

name: Side Plank
summary: Trains the sides of your trunk and hips to hold a straight line.
startingPosition: Lie on your side on a mat with your bottom elbow directly under your shoulder, forearm pointing forward. Legs straight and stacked, or top foot just in front for balance. Hips stacked, head in line with your spine, eyes forward.
steps: Lie on your side with your bottom elbow directly under your shoulder and your legs stacked.
Press your forearm into the floor and lift your hips until you're straight from head to feet, or head to knees with knees bent.
Keep your top hip stacked over your bottom hip, without rolling back or sagging toward the floor.
Hold for the target time with steady breathing, then lower your hips with control.
Roll onto your other side and hold for the same time.

phases.label: Set up
phases.text: Take about 5 seconds to set your elbow under your shoulder and stack your hips on top of each other.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Lift your hips and hold for the target time with steady breaths. End the hold when your hips sag or roll back.

phases.label: Release
phases.text: Lower your hips to the floor over about 2 seconds, then switch sides and hold the other side.

breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily throughout. If you can't breathe without your hips dropping, shorten the hold.
cues: Push the floor away; don't sink into your shoulder.

formChecks.check: Your head, hips and feet form one straight line (head, hips and knees in the bent-knee version), with no droop at the hips.
Your bottom elbow sits directly under your shoulder, so your upper arm is vertical and your neck looks long.
Your chest faces straight ahead, with your top shoulder and hip stacked over the bottom ones, not rolled back.

mistakes.title: Hips sagging
mistakes.looksLike: Your hips drop toward the floor so your body bends sideways into a curve, lower at the hips than at your shoulders and feet.
mistakes.why: The sides of your trunk and hips stop holding you up, and your weight hangs on your shoulder instead.
mistakes.fix: Push your bottom hip up toward the ceiling until head, hips and feet line up. If it keeps sagging, switch to the bent-knee version.
mistakes.cue: Bottom hip up until you're straight.

mistakes.title: Hips rolling or sitting back
mistakes.looksLike: Your top hip rolls back behind the bottom one and your seat drifts behind the line of your shoulders and feet, so you bend at the waist.
mistakes.why: Twisting or bending at the hips takes load off the sides of your trunk, so the hold gets easier but trains less.
mistakes.fix: Stack your top hip over the bottom one and press your hips slightly forward until you're straight. Practicing with your back near a wall helps.
mistakes.cue: Top hip stacked, hips nudged forward.

mistakes.title: Sinking into the shoulder
mistakes.looksLike: Your bottom shoulder hunches up toward your ear and your chest sinks toward the floor, often with the elbow drifting out from under the shoulder.
mistakes.why: Your weight hangs on the shoulder joint instead of the muscles around your shoulder blade holding you up.
mistakes.fix: Set your elbow under your shoulder and push the floor away so your neck looks long. Shorten the hold if you can't keep it.
mistakes.cue: Press the floor away, neck long.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. If your shoulder is uncomfortable, use the bent-knee version or shorten the hold.
On a hard floor, put a mat or folded towel under your elbow, and under your knee for the bent-knee version.
easier: Bend both knees and hold from your bottom knee
harder: Lift your top leg slightly and keep it there

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Lying on one side on a mat, bottom elbow under the shoulder with forearm pointing forward, legs straight and stacked, hip resting on the mat, top hand on the top hip.

frames.label: Hold
frames.pose: Hips lifted so head, shoulders, hips and feet form one straight line; bottom elbow under the shoulder, top hip stacked over the bottom hip, top hand on the hip, gaze forward.

name: Dead Bug
summary: Teaches you to keep your lower back steady while your arms and legs move.
startingPosition: Lie on your back on a mat. Reach both arms straight up over your shoulders. Lift your legs so your hips and knees bend to 90°, knees over hips and shins parallel to the floor. Let your lower back rest gently on the floor.
steps: Lie on your back with your arms pointing at the ceiling and your hips and knees bent to 90°.
Brace your stomach so your lower back rests gently on the floor.
Breathe out as you slowly reach one arm overhead and the opposite leg long toward the floor.
Lower only as far as you can keep your lower back down, then bring the arm and leg back.
Switch to the other arm and leg, alternating until you finish the reps on each side.

phases.label: Reach
phases.text: Breathe out as you lower the opposite arm and leg over 2 to 3 seconds, stopping before your back lifts.

phases.label: Pause
phases.text: Hold the reach for about 1 second with your lower back still touching the floor.

phases.label: Return
phases.text: Bring the arm and leg back over about 2 seconds as you breathe in, then switch sides.

breathing: Breathe out slowly as you reach; it helps keep your ribs down and your back on the floor. Breathe in as you return.
cues: Lower back stays on the floor.
Only as far as you can control.

formChecks.check: Your lower back stays in gentle contact with the floor through the whole reach, with no gap opening underneath.
At the start, your knees are stacked over your hips and your shins are parallel to the floor, both joints at about 90°.
The arm and leg that move are on opposite sides, and your hips stay level without rocking side to side.

mistakes.title: Lower back lifting off the floor
mistakes.looksLike: As the leg lowers, a gap opens between your lower back and the floor and your ribs flare up toward the ceiling.
mistakes.why: Your abs have lost the position, so the leg's weight is arching your spine instead of your trunk resisting it.
mistakes.fix: Reach a shorter distance, keeping the leg higher, and breathe out fully as you reach. Keep the knee bent if a straight leg is too far.
mistakes.cue: Shorter reach, leg higher.

mistakes.title: Head lifting off the floor
mistakes.looksLike: Your head and shoulders curl up off the floor and your chin tucks toward your chest as you reach.
mistakes.why: Curling up turns the move into a crunch. The point is a still trunk while your arms and legs move.
mistakes.fix: Rest your head on the floor with your chin slightly tucked and your eyes on the ceiling. Reach only as far as you can with your head down.
mistakes.cue: Head down, eyes on the ceiling.

mistakes.title: Moving same-side arm and leg
mistakes.looksLike: Your right arm and right leg reach out together, instead of your right arm with your left leg.
mistakes.why: Opposite arm and leg make your trunk resist a diagonal pull, which is the control this exercise trains.
mistakes.fix: Practice the arms alone, then the legs alone, then put them together. Say "right arm, left leg" quietly as you go.
mistakes.cue: Right arm with left leg, then switch.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. If your lower back is uncomfortable, shorten the reach or move only your legs with knees bent.
Keep your head resting on the floor. If your neck feels strained, put a thin folded towel under your head.
easier: Keep knees bent and tap one heel down at a time
harder: Hollow Hold

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Lying on the back on a mat, both arms reaching straight up over the shoulders, hips and knees bent to 90° with shins parallel to the floor, lower back resting on the mat.

frames.label: Reach
frames.pose: One arm reaching overhead just above the mat, opposite leg straightened and hovering a little above the mat, other arm and leg still in the start position, lower back flat on the mat.

name: Bird Dog
summary: Teaches you to keep your trunk still while you reach an arm and a leg.
startingPosition: On hands and knees on a mat, hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips, about hip-width apart. Back flat like a table, neck long, eyes on the floor between your hands.
steps: Set up on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Brace your stomach so your back stays flat and your hips stay level.
Slowly reach one arm forward and the opposite leg straight back, long rather than high, to about the height of your back.
Pause for a breath without letting your hips tip or turn, then bring the hand and knee back under you.
Switch sides and alternate until you finish the reps on each side.

phases.label: Reach
phases.text: Reach the opposite arm and leg out long over about 2 seconds, no higher than your back.

phases.label: Pause
phases.text: Hold for about 2 seconds with your hips level and your trunk still.

phases.label: Return
phases.text: Bring the hand and knee back under you over about 2 seconds, then switch sides.

breathing: Breathe out as you reach and breathe in as you return, keeping your stomach braced throughout.
cues: Glass of water on your lower back.
Push the floor away with your standing hand.

formChecks.check: At full reach, your arm, back and lifted leg form one long line close to level, with no dip in your lower back.
Both sides of your pelvis stay at the same height as the leg lifts, with no tilt or turn toward the ceiling.
Before each rep, your hands are under your shoulders and your knees are under your hips.

mistakes.title: Lifting the leg too high
mistakes.looksLike: Your foot rises above hip height and your lower back dips into an arch, with your seat tilting up.
mistakes.why: The lift is coming from arching your back, not from your hips and trunk holding still.
mistakes.fix: Reach your heel straight back, about level with your hip. Think "long" rather than "high".
mistakes.cue: Heel back, level with your hip.

mistakes.title: Hips tipping or twisting
mistakes.looksLike: As the leg lifts, that side's hip rises and turns toward the ceiling, and your trunk tilts toward the supporting knee.
mistakes.why: Turning lets the movement escape through your hips, so your trunk isn't practicing resisting rotation.
mistakes.fix: Imagine a glass of water on your lower back and don't spill it. Reach a shorter distance until your hips stay level.
mistakes.cue: Shorter reach until hips stay level.

mistakes.title: Head lifting to look ahead
mistakes.looksLike: Your head tips back so your eyes look ahead instead of at the floor, and your neck bends back as your arm reaches.
mistakes.why: Craning your neck breaks the long line from head to heel, and it often pulls your lower back into an arch too.
mistakes.fix: Keep your eyes on the floor between your hands so your head stays in line with your back.
mistakes.cue: Eyes on the floor, head in line.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. If your knees are sore, kneel on a folded mat or towel.
If your wrists are uncomfortable, rest on your knuckles with loose fists, or hold dumbbells as handles.
If balancing is hard, reach only an arm or only a leg until you feel steady.
easier: Reach only an arm or only a leg at a time
harder: Pause for three seconds at full reach

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: On hands and knees on a mat, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, back flat like a table, neck long, gaze at the floor.

frames.label: Reach
frames.pose: Same base; one arm reaching forward at shoulder height and the opposite leg reaching straight back at hip height, arm, back and leg in one level line, hips level.

name: Prone Back Extension
summary: Trains the muscles along your spine with a small, controlled chest lift.
startingPosition: Lie face down on a mat, legs straight and about hip-width apart, tops of your feet on the floor. Arms by your sides, palms down. Forehead resting on the mat, chin gently tucked.
steps: Lie face down with your legs straight and your arms by your sides, palms down.
Tuck your chin slightly and squeeze your glutes.
Lift your chest just a few centimeters off the floor, keeping your eyes on the floor.
Pause briefly at the top without cranking any higher.
Lower your chest to the floor with control, keeping your feet down throughout.

phases.label: Lift
phases.text: Raise your chest a few centimeters over about 2 seconds, glutes squeezed and eyes down.

phases.label: Pause
phases.text: Hold the small lift for 1 to 2 seconds without arching any higher.

phases.label: Lower
phases.text: Lower your chest to the mat over about 2 seconds and relax for a breath.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift and breathe in as you lower. Keep breathing during the pause.
cues: Small lift, just a few centimeters.
Chin tucked, eyes on the floor.
Long spine, not a big arch.

formChecks.check: At the top only your upper chest and shoulders clear the mat; your lower ribs stay close to it, with no deep bend at the lower back.
Your neck stays in line with your back: chin tucked and eyes on the floor, not looking ahead.
Your feet stay on the floor and your legs stay straight throughout.

mistakes.title: Arching up too high
mistakes.looksLike: You crank up until your chest is well off the mat and your lower back folds into a deep bend, with your ribs lifting off the floor.
mistakes.why: Past a small lift, your spine is bending to its end range instead of your back muscles controlling a steady position.
mistakes.fix: Lift only a few centimeters, about an inch or two. Stop where your lower ribs stay near the mat, and own that range.
mistakes.cue: Lift an inch or two, ribs near the mat.

mistakes.title: Head and neck cranking up
mistakes.looksLike: Your chin juts forward and up so you're looking at the wall ahead, with a sharp bend at the back of your neck.
mistakes.why: Your neck leads the movement instead of your back muscles, so the effort ends up in the wrong place.
mistakes.fix: Tuck your chin slightly and keep your eyes on the floor a little in front of you. Lead the lift with your chest.
mistakes.cue: Lead with your chest, chin tucked.

mistakes.title: Jerking up with momentum
mistakes.looksLike: You throw your chest up in a quick jerk, sometimes with your feet lifting too, then drop straight back down.
mistakes.why: Momentum does the lift, so the muscles along your spine get very little time working.
mistakes.fix: Count two seconds up, a short pause, and two seconds down. Keep your feet on the floor and your glutes squeezed.
mistakes.cue: Two seconds up, pause, two down.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. If your lower back feels pinched at the top, lift less.
On a hard floor, put a mat or folded towel under your hips.
easier: Lift less and skip the pause at the top
harder: Hands lightly at your temples, or a 3-second pause

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Lying face down on a mat, legs straight and hip-width apart, arms along the sides with palms down, forehead resting on the mat.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Upper chest and shoulders lifted a few centimeters off the mat, lower ribs and hips on the mat, chin tucked, gaze at the floor, arms by the sides, feet on the floor.

name: Bear Plank
summary: Teaches you to hold a flat, braced back with your knees hovering.
startingPosition: On hands and knees, hands under your shoulders with fingers spread, knees under your hips about hip-width apart, toes tucked under. Back flat like a table, neck long, eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands.
steps: Set up on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Tuck your toes under and brace your stomach so your back is flat like a table.
Press into your hands and toes to lift your knees about 2–5 cm (an inch or two) off the floor.
Hold the hover with steady breathing, keeping your back flat and your hips level.
Lower your knees gently to the floor at the end of the hold.

phases.label: Set up
phases.text: Take about 5 seconds to line up your hands and knees, tuck your toes and brace.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Hover your knees and hold for the target time, breathing steadily. End the hold when your hips rise or your back loses its flat shape.

phases.label: Release
phases.text: Lower your knees to the floor over about 2 seconds, then rest.

breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily the whole time, keeping your stomach firm. If you're holding your breath, shorten the hold.

formChecks.check: Your knees hover only 2–5 cm off the floor, directly under your hips, and your back is flat from shoulders to hips.
Your hands are under your shoulders so your arms are vertical, and your hips are about level with your shoulders.
Your head stays in line with your back, eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands.

mistakes.title: Hips shooting up
mistakes.looksLike: Your knees straighten and your hips rise well above your shoulders, so your body forms an upside-down V.
mistakes.why: Raising the hips moves the weight onto your arms and legs, so your trunk has much less to hold.
mistakes.fix: Keep your knees bent at about 90° and directly under your hips. Hover them only an inch or two off the floor.
mistakes.cue: Knees under hips, hovering low.

mistakes.title: Back rounding or sagging
mistakes.looksLike: Your upper back humps up toward the ceiling, or your lower back dips toward the floor, instead of staying flat.
mistakes.why: Your trunk is changing shape instead of holding it, and holding that shape is what this exercise trains.
mistakes.fix: Brace your stomach and imagine a tray balanced flat on your back. Set your knees down and reset if the shape changes.
mistakes.cue: Brace; balance a tray on your back.

mistakes.title: Hands too far forward
mistakes.looksLike: Your hands sit well in front of your shoulders, so your arms slant forward and your hips sink back toward your heels.
mistakes.why: The support moves out from under you, so your shoulders take the strain and your trunk does less of the bracing.
mistakes.fix: Set your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips before you lift your knees.
mistakes.cue: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. If your wrists are uncomfortable, make fists or hold dumbbell handles so your wrists stay straight.
If your knees or hips feel uncomfortable in the hover, set your knees down more often and shorten each hold.
easier: Hover for 5–10 seconds, then rest and repeat
harder: Slowly tap each shoulder, keeping hips level

frames.label: Start
