frames.pose: On hands and knees on a mat, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, toes tucked under, back flat, gaze at the floor.

frames.label: Hover
frames.pose: Hands under the shoulders, knees bent about 90° and hovering 2–5 cm above the mat directly under the hips, back flat like a table, hips about level with the shoulders, gaze at the floor ahead.

name: Pallof Press
summary: Trains your trunk to resist twisting as a band pulls you to the side.
equipment: resistance band anchored at chest height, to your side
startingPosition: Band anchored at chest height. Stand side-on to the anchor, a step or two away so the band is taut. Feet hip- to shoulder-width apart, knees soft. Both hands hold the band at the middle of your chest. Eyes straight ahead.
steps: Anchor the band at chest height and stand side-on to it, far enough away that the band is taut.
Hold the band with both hands at the center of your chest, feet hip- to shoulder-width apart and knees soft.
Brace and press your hands straight out from your chest until your arms are straight.
Resist the pull toward the anchor so your chest and hips keep facing forward, and pause for a moment.
Bring your hands back to your chest with control.
Finish the reps, then turn to face the other way and repeat on the other side.

phases.label: Press
phases.text: Press your hands straight out from your chest over about 2 seconds without turning.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Hold your arms straight for 1 to 2 seconds, resisting the pull toward the anchor.

phases.label: Return
phases.text: Bring your hands back to your chest over about 2 seconds, still facing forward.

breathing: Breathe out as you press and breathe in as you bring your hands back. Keep breathing during the hold.
cues: Press straight out from your breastbone.
Don't let the band turn you.
Hands stay in front of the middle of your chest.

formChecks.check: Your hands press straight out from the middle of your chest and stay there, without drifting toward the anchor.
With your arms straight, your shoulders and hips stay square to the camera, with no turn toward the anchor.
Your feet stay planted and your trunk stays upright, with no lean or sideways hip shift away from the anchor.

mistakes.title: Twisting toward the anchor
mistakes.looksLike: As your arms straighten, your shoulders and hands rotate toward the anchor, so your chest no longer faces straight ahead.
mistakes.why: The point is to resist rotation. Once you turn, the band has won and your trunk stops working against it.
mistakes.fix: Step closer to the anchor to reduce the tension and press more slowly. Keep your hands in front of the middle of your chest.
mistakes.cue: Step closer in, press more slowly.

mistakes.title: Leaning away from the band
mistakes.looksLike: Your upper body tilts away from the anchor or your hips shift sideways, so you're no longer standing tall over your feet.
mistakes.why: Leaning uses your body weight to counter the pull, instead of your trunk muscles holding you still.
mistakes.fix: Stand tall with your weight even on both feet and your ribs over your hips. Use less band tension if you have to lean.
mistakes.cue: Weight even on both feet, stand tall.

mistakes.title: Arching your lower back
mistakes.looksLike: As your arms go out, your ribs lift, your lower back arches and your hips push forward.
mistakes.why: The arch lets your back take over, and your abs lose the braced position that resists the pull.
mistakes.fix: Tuck your ribs down and squeeze your glutes before each press. Keep your knees soft and your stance steady.
mistakes.cue: Tuck ribs, squeeze glutes, then press.

safety: Check that the band is firmly anchored and not frayed before each set, and keep your face out of its path.
Stop if you feel sharp pain. If you can't stay square, use a lighter band or stand closer to the anchor.
easier: Step closer to the anchor to lower the tension
harder: Step farther from the anchor, or pause 3 seconds out

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing side-on to a band anchored at chest height to one side, feet shoulder-width, knees soft, both hands holding the band at the center of the chest, band taut.

frames.label: Press
frames.pose: Same stance, arms pressed straight out in front of the chest with hands at the midline, chest and hips facing forward, band pulling sideways toward the anchor.

name: Farmer Carry
summary: Trains your grip and posture as you walk tall with a dumbbell in each hand.
equipment: two dumbbells and a clear walkway
startingPosition: Dumbbells on the floor beside your feet, feet hip-width apart. Hinge at the hips with a flat back, bend your knees and grip each handle in the middle. Stand up tall with the dumbbells at your sides, shoulders down and back, eyes ahead.
steps: Stand between the dumbbells, hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip each handle in the middle.
Push through your feet to stand tall with a dumbbell at each side, arms long and shoulders down and back.
Walk with short, steady steps, eyes ahead and trunk upright, turning with small steps at the end of your walkway.
Keep the dumbbells still at your sides, without letting them swing or pull you into a lean.
At the end of the target time, stop, hinge at the hips with a flat back and set the dumbbells down.

phases.label: Pick up
phases.text: Hinge with a flat back and stand up with the dumbbells over about 2 seconds.

phases.label: Walk
phases.text: Walk tall with short, steady steps for the target time, breathing steadily.

phases.label: Set down
phases.text: Stop, hinge at the hips with a flat back and lower the dumbbells to the floor over about 2 seconds.

breathing: Take steady, controlled breaths as you walk, keeping your stomach braced. Don't hold your breath for the whole walk.

formChecks.check: Your ear, shoulder, hip and ankle stack in a vertical line as you walk, with no forward lean or backward arch.
Your shoulders stay level and your trunk stays upright, with no lean toward either dumbbell.
The dumbbells hang still beside your thighs rather than swinging forward and back with each step.

mistakes.title: Shoulders rounding forward
mistakes.looksLike: Your shoulders roll forward and your upper back rounds, so the dumbbells hang in front of your thighs and your head pokes forward.
mistakes.why: Your upper back stops holding your posture, and the weight pulls you out of the tall position the carry trains.
mistakes.fix: Before you walk, stand tall and set your shoulders down and back. Use lighter dumbbells if you can't hold the posture.
mistakes.cue: Shoulders set back before you walk.

mistakes.title: Leaning or swaying
mistakes.looksLike: Your trunk tips to one side or rocks side to side with each step, and one shoulder sits lower than the other.
mistakes.why: Your trunk muscles stop holding you upright, so the weights are moving you instead of you carrying them.
mistakes.fix: Take shorter steps and keep your shoulders level. If one side keeps dropping, use lighter dumbbells or shorten the walk.
mistakes.cue: Shorter steps, shoulders level.

mistakes.title: Dumbbells swinging
mistakes.looksLike: The dumbbells swing forward and back like pendulums, or bump against your legs as you walk.
mistakes.why: Swinging weights aren't under control, and they pull your trunk around with every step.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the handles, keep your arms long and still, and slow down with shorter steps.
mistakes.cue: Arms long and still, grip hard.

safety: Clear your walkway of trip hazards before you start, and walk on a floor that isn't slippery.
Pick up and set down the dumbbells with a flat back. If lifting from the floor is hard, start them on a sturdy box or step.
Stop and set the dumbbells down if your grip starts to slip or you feel sharp pain.
easier: Use lighter dumbbells or shorter walks
harder: Carry one dumbbell only, switching sides halfway

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing tall with a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, arms long, shoulders down and back, feet hip-width apart, gaze ahead.

frames.label: Walk
frames.pose: Mid-step with one foot a short step ahead of the other, trunk upright with ear, shoulder and hip stacked, a dumbbell hanging still beside each thigh, gaze ahead.

name: Hollow Hold
summary: Trains your abs to hold a curved, braced shape with your back pressed down.
startingPosition: Lie on your back on a mat with knees bent, feet flat and arms by your sides. Press your lower back into the mat so there is no gap underneath, and tuck your chin slightly.
steps: Lie on your back and press your lower back into the floor so there is no gap underneath.
Tuck your chin slightly and lift your head and shoulder blades off the floor, arms reaching toward your feet.
Lift your legs with your knees bent and your shins parallel to the floor.
If your back stays down, straighten your legs at a height you can hold.
Hold for the target time, and end the hold as soon as your lower back starts to lift.

phases.label: Set up
phases.text: Take about 5 seconds to press your lower back down, then lift your shoulders and legs.

phases.label: Hold
phases.text: Hold the shape for the target time with steady breaths. End the hold when your lower back starts to lift.

phases.label: Release
phases.text: Lower your head, arms and legs to the floor over about 2 seconds, then rest.

breathing: Take short, steady breaths while your stomach stays braced and your back stays pressed down. Don't hold your breath.
cues: Lower back pressed into the floor.
Reach long through hands and feet.

formChecks.check: There is no gap between your lower back and the floor for the whole hold, and your body makes a shallow, even curve.
Your shoulder blades and legs are both lifted, with your legs at the lowest height you can hold without your back arching.
Your chin is gently tucked with your eyes toward your feet, and your head isn't straining forward.

mistakes.title: Lower back lifting off the floor
mistakes.looksLike: A gap opens between your lower back and the floor and your ribs flare up, usually because your legs are too low.
mistakes.why: Once your back arches, your abs have lost the shape and your lower back is taking the strain instead.
mistakes.fix: Bend your knees or raise your legs higher until your back presses down again. End the hold if it keeps lifting.
mistakes.cue: Legs up until your back presses down.

mistakes.title: Pulling with the neck
mistakes.looksLike: Your chin juts toward the ceiling and your head lifts higher than your shoulders, with the front of your neck straining.
mistakes.why: Your neck is doing the lifting instead of your abs curling your ribs toward your hips.
mistakes.fix: Tuck your chin slightly, as if holding a small ball under it, and lift from your shoulder blades. Rest your head between holds.
mistakes.cue: Hold a small ball under your chin.

mistakes.title: Shoulders flat on the floor
mistakes.looksLike: Only your legs lift while your head and shoulder blades stay on the mat, so your body makes an L shape rather than a curve.
mistakes.why: Without the upper body lifted, your abs don't have to curl from both ends, and it turns mostly into a leg lift.
mistakes.fix: Curl your ribs toward your hips until your shoulder blades just clear the floor, then lift your legs.
mistakes.cue: Curl up until shoulder blades clear.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. If your lower back aches, bend your knees, raise your legs or switch to the dead bug.
If your neck tires, rest your head on the mat between holds and shorten the next hold.
easier: Dead Bug
harder: Reach arms overhead and lower legs, back still down

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Lying on the back on a mat, knees bent with feet flat, arms by the sides, lower back pressed into the mat, chin slightly tucked.

frames.label: Hold
frames.pose: Lower back pressed into the mat, head and shoulder blades lifted, chin tucked, arms reaching toward the feet, legs straight and raised about 45° off the mat, body in a shallow curve.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
summary: Trains the biceps to bend the elbows against load, without swinging.
startingPosition: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees soft. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight by your sides, palms facing forward. Elbows touch your sides, shoulders down, eyes ahead.
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight by your sides and palms facing forward.
Pin your elbows to your sides and brace your stomach lightly.
Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders by bending only at the elbows.
Stop at the highest point you can reach while your elbows still touch your sides.
Lower the dumbbells over two to three seconds until your arms are fully straight.

phases.label: Curling
phases.text: Bend your elbows to bring the dumbbells up in about one second while your upper arms stay still.

phases.label: Top
phases.text: Hold for about one second with your elbows still at your sides.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower the dumbbells over two to three seconds until your arms are fully straight.

breathing: Breathe out as you curl the dumbbells up. Breathe in as you lower them under control.
cues: Lower slowly, all the way to straight.

formChecks.check: Your upper arm stays vertical and against your side from bottom to top; the point of your elbow barely moves forward.
Your torso stays upright all set, with no lean back or hip push as each curl starts.
At the bottom of every rep your elbows are fully straight, dumbbells beside your thighs, before the next curl begins.

mistakes.title: Swinging the torso
mistakes.looksLike: You lean back or thrust your hips forward to get the dumbbells moving, so your torso tips 10° or more behind vertical as they rise.
mistakes.why: Momentum from your hips and back lifts the weight, so your biceps skip the hardest part of the rep.
mistakes.fix: Soften your knees, brace, and keep your torso completely still. If you can't, use lighter dumbbells or stand with your back against a wall.
mistakes.cue: Soft knees, brace, torso stays put.

mistakes.title: Elbows drifting forward
mistakes.looksLike: As the dumbbells rise, your elbows slide forward and up, so at the top your upper arms point 30° or more in front of your body.
mistakes.why: Your front shoulders start lifting, and the weight ends up stacked over your elbows, where your biceps barely have to work.
mistakes.fix: Keep your elbows touching your sides and end the curl where they would have to move to go higher. Picture your upper arms pinned in place.
mistakes.cue: Upper arms pinned to your sides.

mistakes.title: Cutting the bottom short
mistakes.looksLike: You drop the dumbbells quickly and start the next curl with your elbows still bent around 30°, never reaching straight arms.
mistakes.why: You skip the stretched bottom of the rep, where your biceps work hard, and lose the controlled lowering half of every rep.
mistakes.fix: Count two to three seconds on the way down and let your elbows straighten fully, dumbbells by your thighs, before each curl.
mistakes.cue: Elbows fully straight at the bottom.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your elbow, wrist or shoulder. Lighter dumbbells or a shorter range are fine while you learn.
If your wrists ache with palms facing up, turn your palms partly inward toward a hammer grip.
Pick a weight you can curl on every rep without leaning back, even if it feels light.
easier: Use lighter dumbbells, back against a wall
harder: Lower each rep over four seconds

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Standing tall, feet hip-width, knees soft, arms straight by the sides, a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing forward, elbows touching the sides.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Same upright stance; elbows still touching the sides, forearms close to vertical, dumbbells near shoulder height, palms facing the shoulders, wrists straight.

name: Hammer Curl
summary: Trains the biceps and forearms with a neutral, palms-in grip.
startingPosition: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees soft. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your thighs, thumbs pointing forward. Elbows touch your sides, shoulders down, eyes ahead.
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight by your sides and palms facing each other.
Pin your elbows to your sides and brace your stomach lightly.
Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, thumbs leading, bending only at the elbows.
Stop at the highest point you can reach while your elbows still touch your sides.
Lower over two to three seconds until your arms are fully straight, palms still facing in.

phases.label: Curling
phases.text: Bend your elbows to bring the dumbbells up in about one second, thumbs leading and upper arms still.

phases.label: Top
phases.text: Hold for about one second with your elbows still at your sides.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower over two to three seconds until your arms are fully straight.

breathing: Breathe out as you curl the dumbbells up. Breathe in as you lower them under control.

formChecks.check: Neither dumbbell ever turns crosswise, as it would in a palms-up curl; your palms keep facing each other from bottom to top.
Your upper arm stays vertical against your side; the point of your elbow barely moves forward as the dumbbell rises.
Your torso stays upright, and your arms reach fully straight at the bottom of every rep.

mistakes.title: Swinging the torso
mistakes.looksLike: You rock back or snap your hips forward to start each curl, so your torso tips 10° or more behind vertical as the dumbbells rise.
mistakes.why: Your hips and back supply the momentum, so your biceps and forearms do less of the lifting.
mistakes.fix: Soften your knees, brace, and keep your torso still from the first rep to the last. If you can't, use lighter dumbbells.
mistakes.cue: Brace; torso still to the last rep.

mistakes.title: Elbows drifting forward
mistakes.looksLike: Your elbows travel forward and up as you curl, so at the top your upper arms point 30° or more in front of your body.
mistakes.why: Your front shoulders join in, and the dumbbell ends up stacked over the elbow, so your arm muscles get a rest at the top.
mistakes.fix: Keep your elbows touching your sides and end the curl where they would have to move to go higher.
mistakes.cue: Stop the curl before elbows move.

mistakes.title: Stopping short at the bottom
mistakes.looksLike: At the bottom your elbows stay bent at about 90°, so the dumbbells never get back down beside your thighs.
mistakes.why: Skipping the bottom half of each rep trains only part of the movement, so your arms get less work for the same reps.
mistakes.fix: Lower until your arms are straight and the dumbbells hang beside your thighs, then start the next curl.
mistakes.cue: Straight arms at the bottom.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your elbow, wrist or shoulder. Lighter dumbbells or a shorter range are fine while you learn.
Many people find this grip more comfortable than palms-up curls. Keep your wrists straight, in line with your forearms.
easier: Use lighter dumbbells and stand against a wall
harder: Pause one second with forearms level

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Standing tall, feet hip-width, knees soft, arms straight by the sides, a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing the thighs and thumbs forward, elbows touching the sides.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Same upright stance; elbows still touching the sides, forearms close to vertical, palms facing each other, thumbs toward the shoulders, wrists straight.

name: Band Biceps Curl
summary: Trains the biceps against a band that pulls harder as you curl higher.
startingPosition: Stand on the middle of the band, feet hip-width apart, knees soft. Hold one end in each hand, arms straight by your sides, palms forward, with a little tension in the band. Elbows touch your sides, eyes ahead.
steps: Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip-width apart and hold one end in each hand, palms facing forward.
Pin your elbows to your sides and brace your stomach lightly.
Curl your hands toward your shoulders by bending only at the elbows.
Hold for a moment at the top, where the band pulls hardest.
Lower over two to three seconds, resisting the band, until your arms are fully straight.

phases.label: Curling
phases.text: Bend your elbows to bring your hands up in about one second while your upper arms stay still.

phases.label: Top
phases.text: Hold for about one second against the band's strongest pull.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Resist the band for two to three seconds until your arms are fully straight.

breathing: Breathe out as you curl your hands up. Breathe in as you lower them against the band.
cues: Fight the band on the way down.
Arms fully straight at the bottom.

formChecks.check: Your upper arms stay vertical against your sides; your elbows do not move forward as the band tightens near the top.
Your torso stays upright with no lean back, even on the last, hardest reps.
Both feet stay flat on the band, hip-width apart, and both hands rise and lower together at the same speed.

mistakes.title: Leaning back near the top
mistakes.looksLike: As the band gets tight near the top, your torso tips back 10° or more or your hips push forward to finish the rep.
mistakes.why: Your back and hips finish the curl, so your biceps skip the top of the rep, where the band pulls hardest.
mistakes.fix: Keep your torso still to the last rep. Use a lighter band, or bring your feet closer together on the band to ease the tension.
mistakes.cue: Feet closer on the band, torso still.

mistakes.title: Elbows drifting forward
mistakes.looksLike: Near the top your elbows slide forward and up, so your upper arms end up angled 30° or more in front of your body.
mistakes.why: Your front shoulders help lift, and the band's pull lines up with your forearms, taking work off your biceps.
mistakes.fix: Keep your elbows touching your sides and end the curl where they would have to move to go higher.
mistakes.cue: Curl only as high as elbows stay put.

mistakes.title: Stopping short at the bottom
mistakes.looksLike: Your hands only come down to about waist height and your elbows stay bent at about 90°, so your arms never straighten between reps.
mistakes.why: Skipping the bottom half of each rep trains only part of the movement, so your arms get less work for the same reps.
mistakes.fix: Lower until your arms are straight by your sides, then curl again. Stand with your feet a little closer on the band if the bottom feels too hard.
mistakes.cue: Straight arms at the bottom.

safety: Check the band for nicks or tears before each session, and keep it firmly under the middle of both feet.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in your elbow, wrist or shoulder. A lighter band or a shorter range is fine while you learn.
easier: Use a lighter band or narrow your stance
harder: Use a heavier band or widen your stance

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Standing tall on the middle of a resistance band, feet hip-width, arms straight by the sides holding the band ends, palms forward, elbows touching the sides, band slightly taut.

frames.label: Top
frames.pose: Same upright stance on the band; elbows still touching the sides, forearms close to vertical, hands near the shoulders, band stretched taut from the feet to the hands.

name: Band Triceps Pushdown
summary: Trains the triceps to straighten the elbows against a band.
startingPosition: Face the door with the band anchored high, feet hip-width, knees soft, torso upright or leaning slightly forward. Hold the band with both hands, elbows pinned to your sides and bent about 90°, forearms level, shoulders down.
steps: Anchor the band high on a door and stand facing it, holding the band with both hands.
Step back until the band is slightly taut with your elbows pinned to your sides and bent about 90°.
Press your hands down until your arms are straight, moving only your forearms.
Pause for a moment with your arms straight and your hands by your thighs.
Let your hands rise over two to three seconds until your forearms are about level with the floor.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Push your hands down in about one second until your arms are straight.

phases.label: Lockout
phases.text: Hold the straight-arm position for about one second, hands by your thighs.

phases.label: Return
phases.text: Let your hands rise over two to three seconds, elbows still at your sides, until your forearms are level.

breathing: Breathe out as you press the band down. Breathe in as your hands rise back up.
cues: Press all the way to straight.
Chest up; don't lean over your hands.

formChecks.check: Your upper arms stay vertical against your sides; your elbows don't swing forward on the way up or back on the way down.
At the bottom your elbows are fully straight, with your hands beside the front of your thighs.
Your torso angle stays the same all set, upright or slightly forward, and never folds over your hands to finish a rep.

mistakes.title: Leaning over the hands
mistakes.looksLike: To finish each rep you fold forward at the hips, bringing your chest over your hands and pushing your body weight down onto the band.
mistakes.why: Your body weight and shoulders press the band down, so your triceps do only part of the work.
mistakes.fix: Set your torso upright, or with a slight forward lean, before the first rep and hold it. Only your forearms move. Use a lighter band if needed.
mistakes.cue: Set your torso upright and hold it.

mistakes.title: Upper arms swinging
mistakes.looksLike: Your elbows drift forward as your hands rise and swing back as you press, so your upper arms move like a pendulum instead of staying vertical.
mistakes.why: Moving at the shoulder turns the rep into a pulldown, so your back and shoulders help and your triceps do less.
mistakes.fix: Keep your elbows touching your sides. Let your hands rise only until your forearms are level, then press back down.
mistakes.cue: Elbows still, forearms up to level.

mistakes.title: Stopping short of straight
mistakes.looksLike: You press only partway, stopping with your elbows still bent 20–30° before letting the band pull your hands back up.
mistakes.why: The band pulls hardest as your arms reach straight, so stopping short skips the part where your triceps work most.
mistakes.fix: Press until your elbows are fully straight and pause for a moment. If you can't reach straight arms, use a lighter band.
mistakes.cue: Elbows fully straight, brief pause.

safety: Anchor the band in a closed door that opens away from you, and check the band for nicks or tears before you start.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in your elbow or shoulder. A lighter band or a shorter range is fine while you learn.
easier: Use a lighter band or step closer to the door
harder: Step farther back or use a heavier band

frames.label: Start
frames.pose: Standing facing a door with a band anchored at the top, torso upright, elbows pinned to the sides and bent about 90°, forearms level with the floor, both hands holding the band.

frames.label: Lockout
frames.pose: Same stance and torso angle; elbows still at the sides, arms fully straight, hands beside the front of the thighs, band stretched from the top of the door to the hands.

name: Overhead Triceps Extension
summary: Trains the triceps through a long range, with the arms overhead.
startingPosition: Sit tall on a sturdy chair, feet flat and hip-width apart. Hold one dumbbell overhead, both palms cupping the top plate, thumbs and fingers in a diamond around the handle. Arms straight, upper arms by your ears, ribs down.
steps: Sit tall on a sturdy chair with your feet flat and hip-width apart.
Hold one dumbbell upright by its top plate, both hands forming a diamond around the handle, and press it overhead.
Point your elbows forward and up, keep your upper arms close to your head, and pull your ribs down.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head over two to three seconds.
Straighten your arms to press the dumbbell back overhead, keeping your upper arms still.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head over two to three seconds, upper arms still.

phases.label: Bottom
phases.text: Pause for about one second with your elbows pointing forward and up.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Straighten your arms in one to two seconds to bring the dumbbell back overhead.

breathing: Breathe in as you lower the dumbbell behind your head. Breathe out as you press it back up, keeping your ribs down.

formChecks.check: Your elbows stay about shoulder-width apart or narrower, pointing forward and up, never flaring wider than your shoulders.
Your upper arms stay close to vertical beside your head while only your forearms move, and your elbows bend to about 90° or a little more.
Your lower back keeps the same gentle curve it had at the start; your ribs don't flare forward as the dumbbell goes down.

mistakes.title: Elbows flaring out
mistakes.looksLike: As the dumbbell lowers, your elbows splay out to the sides until they are well wider than your shoulders, so your upper arms form a wide V.
mistakes.why: The dumbbell's path gets harder to control, and your triceps get less of the long, stretched range this exercise is for.
mistakes.fix: Point your elbows forward and up, about shoulder-width apart. If your shoulders won't allow it, use a lighter dumbbell and a shorter range.
mistakes.cue: Elbows about shoulder-width apart.

mistakes.title: Arching the lower back
mistakes.looksLike: As the dumbbell goes overhead or behind your head, your ribs flare forward and your lower back arches, tipping your torso back off vertical.
mistakes.why: Your back makes room for the weight instead of your shoulders, and the rep becomes harder to control.
mistakes.fix: Breathe in, brace, and keep your ribs pulled down toward your hips. Use a lighter dumbbell if the arch keeps coming back.
mistakes.cue: Brace and pull ribs toward your hips.

mistakes.title: Upper arms dropping forward
mistakes.looksLike: Your upper arms tip forward as you lower the weight and swing back as you press, so the dumbbell moves in an arc in front of your face.
mistakes.why: Moving at the shoulder lets other muscles help and shortens the triceps' stretch, so the triceps do less of the work.
mistakes.fix: Keep your upper arms close to your head and still; only your elbows bend. Lower only as far as you can without your elbows dropping.
mistakes.cue: Upper arms still beside your head.

safety: Lift the dumbbell to your chest first, then press it overhead with both hands. Use one you can control easily behind your head.
If your shoulders or elbows ache overhead, shorten the range or swap to the band triceps pushdown.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in your elbow or shoulder.
easier: Use a lighter dumbbell and a shorter range
harder: Lower over four seconds and pause at the bottom

frames.label: Bottom
frames.pose: Same seated posture; upper arms still beside the head with elbows pointing forward and up, elbows bent a little past 90°, dumbbell lowered behind the head toward the upper back.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
summary: Trains the side shoulders by raising the arms out to the sides.
startingPosition: Stand tall, feet hip-width, knees soft, torso upright or leaning slightly forward. Hold a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms in, elbows slightly bent. Shoulders down, away from your ears, eyes ahead.
steps: Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Soften your elbows into a slight bend and keep that bend the whole set.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides, leading with your elbows, until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Stop at shoulder height with your shoulders down and the dumbbells level.
Lower over two to three seconds until the dumbbells are back by your sides.

phases.label: Raising
phases.text: Lift the dumbbells out to the sides in one to two seconds, elbows leading, until your arms are parallel to the floor.

phases.label: Top
phases.text: Hold for about one second at shoulder height with your shoulders down.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower the dumbbells over two to three seconds back to your sides.

breathing: Breathe out as you raise the dumbbells. Breathe in as you lower them slowly.
cues: Shoulders down, away from your ears.

formChecks.check: At the top your arms are about parallel to the floor, elbows level with or slightly above your hands, and nothing above shoulder height.
The gap between your shoulders and ears stays the same from bottom to top; your shoulders don't hike toward your ears.
At the top each dumbbell is level, or its thumb end slightly lower, and your torso keeps the same slight lean with no rocking.

mistakes.title: Shrugging the shoulders
mistakes.looksLike: As the dumbbells rise, your shoulders hike up toward your ears and the gap between shoulder and ear shrinks, often more on the last reps.
mistakes.why: Your upper traps take over the lift, so your side shoulders do less of the work you are after.
mistakes.fix: Set your shoulders down before each rep and think "reach out to the walls", not up. Use lighter dumbbells.
mistakes.cue: Reach out to the walls, not up.

mistakes.title: Swinging the weights up
mistakes.looksLike: You dip your knees or rock your torso back to start each rep, and the dumbbells fly up fast instead of rising steadily.
mistakes.why: Momentum lifts the weight, so your side shoulders skip the start of the rep and you lose control at the top.
mistakes.fix: Hold a slight forward lean, keep your knees still, and raise in about one to two seconds. If you have to swing, the dumbbells are too heavy.
mistakes.cue: Knees still, slow steady raise.

mistakes.title: Raising above the shoulders
mistakes.looksLike: Your hands finish above shoulder height, with your arms angled up past parallel to the floor, often with a shrug to get there.
mistakes.why: Above shoulder height your upper traps take more of the work, and your side shoulders gain little.
mistakes.fix: Stop when your arms are parallel to the floor. Picture a shelf at shoulder height and touch it with your elbows.
mistakes.cue: Arms stop parallel to the floor.

mistakes.title: Turning the thumbs up
mistakes.looksLike: Your hands lead and rise higher than your elbows, thumbs tipped up, and the dumbbells drift forward toward a front raise.
mistakes.why: Turning the thumbs up and bringing the arms forward shifts the work toward your front shoulders.
mistakes.fix: Lead with your elbows and keep the dumbbells level at the top. Thumbs level with or slightly below your little fingers is fine.
mistakes.cue: Thumbs level with your little fingers.

safety: Start light; this exercise needs far less weight than pressing. Stop if you feel sharp or pinching pain in your shoulder.
If shoulder height feels pinchy, raise only as high as is comfortable, or angle your arms slightly forward of your sides.
easier: Use lighter dumbbells or bend your elbows more
harder: Pause for one second at shoulder height
